Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 1–2:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿By the star when it sets (1), your companion has neither strayed nor erred (2)﴾

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words ﴿By the star when it sets﴾. Some of them said: by "the star" is meant the Pleiades (al-Thurayya), and by His words ﴿when it sets﴾ is meant: when it falls. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "By the Pleiades when they fall."

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words (﴿By the star when it sets﴾), he said: "When the Pleiades fall at dawn."

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, ﴿By the star when it sets﴾, he said: "The Pleiades." And Mujahid said: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾, he said: "The falling of the Pleiades."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾, he said: "When it pours down."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "By the Qur'an when it is sent down."

Mention of those who said this:

Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hassani Abu al-Khattab related to me, he said: Malik ibn Su'ayr related to us, he said: al-A'mash related to us, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿By the star when it sets﴾, he said: "The Qur'an when it is sent down."

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has neither strayed nor erred﴾, he said: "'Utbah ibn Abi Lahab said: 'I have disbelieved in the Lord of the star.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Do you not fear that the dog of Allah will devour you?' He went out on a trade journey to Yemen, and while they were camping, he heard the sound of a lion. He said to his companions: 'I am going to be eaten.' So they encircled him and struck their ears, and they slept. [The lion] came and seized him, and they heard nothing but its roar."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, he said: Ma'mar related to us, from Qatadah: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) recited ﴿By the star when it sets﴾, and the son of Abu Lahab – I think he said his name was 'Utbah – said: 'I have disbelieved in the Lord of the star.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Beware, lest the dog of Allah devour you.'" He said: "[The Prophet] struck his head." He said: Ibn Tawus related from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you not fear that Allah will set His dog upon you?" So Ibn Abi Lahab went out with some people on a journey, and when they were on part of the road they heard the sound of a lion. He said: "It is only me that it wants." So his companions gathered around him and placed him in their midst, until when they slept, the lion came and seized him from among them.

Some of the scholars of the Arabic language among the people of Basra used to say: by His words ﴿By the star﴾ is meant "the stars" (al-nujum). He said: he went to the singular form, while in meaning it is plural, and he cited as evidence for this the words of the camel herder:

"So she spent the night counting the star in a bowl that was filled [with fat], [its] congealed [fat] quickly taken by the hands of those who eat."

[The verse is by the camel herder (rā'ī al-ibil) al-Numayri, ʿUbayd ibn Ayyub. (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda, folio 230.) He said regarding the verse ﴿By the star when it sets﴾: an oath; "al-najm" means "the stars"; he went to the singular form while meaning the plural. The camel herder said: "And she spent the night counting the star…" the verse. "Mustahayyira" means containing fat (ihāla); he made it floating because it is fat. Ibn Qutayba said in al-Ma'ani al-Kabir (printed in India): The camel herder, mentioning a woman whom he was entertaining, said: "So she spent the night…" the verse. "Mustahayyira": a bowl in which the fat has become a pool, so she sees the stars in it because of the clarity of the fat. By his words "she counts the star" he meant the Pleiades, and the Arabs call the Pleiades "the star." He said: "The star rose at nightfall… the herder sought a cloak."

Al-Tabrizi said in his commentary on the Hamasa of Abu Tammam (4:39): Abu al-'Ala' said: some people made "ta'uddu" here from counting, meaning this woman counts the stars in the bowl that is "mustahayyira," i.e. full, because she sees the reflections of the stars in it. This reading is permissible, and it may also be that "ta'uddu" means "to reckon and suppose," and the meaning is that the woman supposes the star to be in the bowl because of the whiteness of the fat. End of quotation.]

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is what Mujahid said: that by "the star" in this place is meant the Pleiades, because the Arabs call it "the star." As for the view of those from the people of Basra whom we have quoted, it is a view that we know none of the people of interpretation to have held; although it may have some basis, we have therefore left off adopting it.

* *

And His words: ﴿Your companion has neither strayed nor erred﴾

He, mighty is His remembrance, says: your companion, O people, has not deviated from the truth nor turned away from it, but is upon uprightness and rectitude.

By His words ﴿nor erred﴾ is meant: nor has he become one who is misguided, but he is rightly guided and upright. It is said: "ghawa yaghwa" from error (al-ghayy), and he is "ghaw" (one who errs); and "ghawiya yaghwa" from milk [[In Lisan al-'Arab (root gh-w-y): "ghawa" with a fatha means ghayy; "ghawa" with a kasra, ghiwaya — the latter from Abu 'Ubayda — means "to go astray." And in it: the young camel or the lamb "yaghwa ghawan" (like "fariha") means it became full of milk.]] when it is satiated.

* *

And His words: ﴿Your companion has not strayed﴾

It is the answer to the oath "by the star."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verse 3–7:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed, taught to him by one intense in strength, of soundness and balance. And he was in the highest horizon.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Muhammad does not speak this Qur'an from his own desire (﴿It is not but a revelation revealed﴾), meaning: this Qur'an is nothing but a revelation from God which He reveals to him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾: that is, he does not speak from his desire ﴿It is not but a revelation revealed﴾. He said: God, blessed and exalted, reveals to Jibril, and Jibril reveals to Muhammad ﷺ.

It was also said: by His saying ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ is meant desire (al-hawa).

* *

As for His saying ﴿Taught to him by one intense in strength﴾:

He, exalted is His mention, says: Jibril, peace be upon him, taught Muhammad ﷺ this Qur'an. By His saying ﴿intense in strength﴾ is meant intense in means (al-asbab). Al-quwa is the plural of quwwah (strength), as al-jutha is the plural of juthwah, and al-hiba is the plural of hiba. Some of the Arabs say al-qiwa with a kasra on the qaf, just as al-rishwa (bribe) is pluralized as rishan with a kasra on the ra'. It has been reported from the Arabs that they say rushwah with a damma on the ra' and rishwah with a kasra; so whoever pluralized it with a kasra on the ra' does so according to the dialect of one who says its singular is rishwah, and whoever pluralized it with a damma does so according to the dialect of one who uses a damma in its singular. Whoever pluralizes with a kasra while his dialect has a damma in the singular, or with a damma while his dialect has a kasra, is only applying one dialect to the other.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿taught to him by one intense in strength﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿taught to him by one intense in strength﴾: meaning Jibril.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿taught to him by one intense in strength﴾: he said, Jibril, peace be upon him.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Of soundness and balance﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿dhu mirrah﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: possessor of a good form.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿dhu mirrah﴾: he said, possessor of a good appearance.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: possessor of a tall, good form.

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: possessor of strength.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: he said, possessor of the strength of Jibril.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, ﴿dhu mirrah﴾: he said, possessor of strength.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: he said, possessor of strength; al-mirrah is the strength.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: Jibril, peace be upon him.

The more correct of the two opinions concerning this, in our view, is the opinion of the one who said: by al-mirrah is meant soundness of the body and its freedom from defects and afflictions. When a person's body is so, he is strong. We have said that this is so because mirrah is the singular of mirar, and what is intended is: possessor of a balanced, sound constitution. When the mirrah is sound, the person is sound. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Charity is not lawful for a wealthy person, nor for one who possesses a sound constitution (dhi mirrah sawiyy)."

* *

As for His saying ﴿So he stood, and he was in the highest horizon﴾

He says: this intense and strong one stood, and your companion Muhammad was in the highest horizon. That was when the Messenger of God ﷺ was taken on the night journey: he and Jibril, peace be upon them both, stood at the rising place of the sun, the highest horizon. He linked His saying "wa huwa" (and he) to the mention of Muhammad ﷺ within His saying "fastawa" (so he stood). The majority of Arabic speech, when they wish to conjoin in such a position, bring out an explicit pronoun for the element conjoined upon, saying: "istawa huwa wa fulan" (he stood, he and so-and-so), and they rarely say "istawa wa fulan" (stood and so-and-so). Al-Farra' reported from some Arabs that he recited to him:

Did you not see that the nab' (a hard mountain tree) is firm in its wood, while the kharrub (a soft, easily broken shrub) that snaps does not stand equal?

[This verse is among al-Farra's evidences in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 314), and in his narration the word is "yakhluq" in place of "yaslub". Al-kharrub is a tree with flexible branches, whose twigs snap easily because of their softness, and from its fruit castor oil is extracted, used for medical and industrial purposes. The nab' is a hard tree that grows on mountain heights, from whose wood bows and arrows are made. Between it and the kharrub there is a great difference in the firmness of wood. Al-Farra' cited the verse at His saying "fastawa wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la," meaning: "istawa (huwa)," that is Jibril, and "huwa," that is Muhammad ﷺ, "bil-ufuq al-a'la." He conjoined the explicit "huwa" to the concealed "huwa," so the noun was concealed in istawa, and "huwa" was returned to it. He said: most of the speech of the Arabs is that they say "istawa huwa wa abuhu" (he stood, he and his father); they hardly say "istawa wa abuhu" (stood and his father), though it is permissible because there is a concealed element in the verb. One of them recited to me: "Did you not see that the nab' ..." the verse. And God, who is most truthful in speech, said: (When we are dust and our fathers?) so He returned "ababa" (fathers) to the concealed pronoun in "kunna," except that it is good because it was separated by "turab" (dust); the meaning being: when we are dust, we and our fathers? End of quotation.]

So the kharrub is returned to the "ma" in "yastawi" from the mention of the nab'. From this is His saying ﴿When we are dust and our fathers?﴾, where "al-aba'" is conjoined to the pronoun in "kunna" without explicit "nahnu." Likewise His saying ﴿fastawa wa huwa﴾. It has also been said that the one who stood is Jibril. If that is so, there is no difficulty, because His saying "wa huwa" refers to Jibril's name, and the speaker of this view takes the meaning of His saying "fastawa" as: he rose and became balanced.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: Jibril, peace be upon him.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: and al-ufuq is that from which the day comes.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: he said, at the highest horizon of the east, between them.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: meaning Jibril.

[Ibn Humayd] said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: he said, the highest sky, meaning Jibril, peace be upon him.

Al-kharrub is a tree with flexible branches, whose twigs snap easily because of their softness, and from its fruit castor oil is extracted, used for medical and industrial purposes. The nab' is a hard tree that grows on mountain heights, from whose wood bows and arrows are made. Between it and the kharrub there is a great difference in the firmness of wood. Al-Farra' cited the verse at His saying "fastawa wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la," meaning: "istawa (huwa)," that is Jibril, and "huwa," that is Muhammad ﷺ, "bil-ufuq al-a'la." He conjoined the explicit "huwa" to the concealed "huwa," so the noun was concealed in istawa, and "huwa" was returned to it. He said: most of the speech of the Arabs is that they say "istawa huwa wa abuhu" (he stood, he and his father); they hardly say "istawa wa abuhu" (stood and his father), though it is permissible because there is a concealed element in the verb. One of them recited to me: "Did you not see that the nab' ..." the verse. And God, who is most truthful in speech, said: (When we are dust and our fathers?) so He returned "ababa" (fathers) to the concealed pronoun in "kunna," except that it is good because it was separated by "turab" (dust); the meaning being: when we are dust, we and our fathers? End of quotation.]

So the kharrub is returned to the "ma" in "yastawi" from the mention of the nab'. From this is His saying ﴿When we are dust and our fathers?﴾, where "al-aba'" is conjoined to the pronoun in "kunna" without explicit "nahnu." Likewise His saying ﴿fastawa wa huwa﴾. It has also been said that the one who stood is Jibril. If that is so, there is no difficulty, because His saying "wa huwa" refers to Jibril's name, and the speaker of this view takes the meaning of His saying "fastawa" as: he rose and became balanced.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿dhu mirrah fastawa﴾: Jibril, peace be upon him.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: and al-ufuq is that from which the day comes.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: he said, at the highest horizon of the east, between them.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: meaning Jibril.

[Ibn Humayd] said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', ﴿wa huwa bil-ufuq al-a'la﴾: he said, the highest sky, meaning Jibril, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 8–11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾ [53:8], ﴿and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾ [53:9], ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ [53:10], ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾ [53:11].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then Jibril drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended to him. This is an example of the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) which is meant as the earlier: the meaning is "then he descended and drew near," but the mention of ﴿drew near﴾ first is fine, since drawing near indicates descending and descending indicates drawing near, as one says: "So-and-so visited me and did well [by me]," and "he did well to me and then visited me," and "he insulted me and then did harm," and "he did harm and then insulted me," because harm is insult and insult is harm.

The people of ta'wil (exegesis) said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "Jibril, peace be upon him."

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: meaning Jibril.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "It is Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: then the Lord drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended.

Those who said that:

- Yahya ibn al-Umawi related to us, he said: My father related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "His Lord drew near and descended."

- al-Rabi' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating to us about the night of the Isra' of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Jibril ascended with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the seventh heaven, then he rose with him to a place only Allah knows, until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and the Almighty, Lord of Might, drew near and descended, until there was between him and [Muhammad] two bow-lengths or closer. Then Allah revealed to him what He willed, and among what He revealed was fifty prayers upon his community every day and night," and he mentioned the hadith.

* *

As for His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾:

He says: So Jibril was from Muhammad ﷺ at the measure of two bow-lengths, or closer than that, meaning: nearer. It is said: "He is from him at a distance of qab qawsayn (two bow-lengths), qayb qawsayn, qid qawsayn, qad qawsayn, and qada qawsayn," all of which mean: the measure of two bows.

It was also said that the meaning of His words ﴿qab qawsayn﴾ is that he was at the place of the string on the bow.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "At the place of the string on the bow."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "Qid qawsayn" (the measure of two bows).

Qatadah said the same.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "Qid, or qadr (measure) of two bows."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, drew near to him until he was the measure of one or two cubits."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin regarding ﴿qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "It is not this bow, but the measure of two cubits or closer; and the qab is the qid."

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the referent of His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾. Some of them said, in accordance with what we have said regarding it:

- Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, he said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, he said: Zirr ibn Hubaysh related to us, he said: 'Abd Allah said regarding this verse ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril, he had six hundred wings."

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari related to us, he said: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "Jibril saw six hundred wings in his form."

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: Qabis ibn Layth al-Asadi related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril, peace be upon him, who had six hundred wings."

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The beginning of the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was that he saw Jibril in his dream at Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Jibril called out to him: "O Muhammad!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked right and left but saw nothing, three times. Then he went out and saw him, and he entered among the people, then went out again, or he said: then he looked, "I am unsure," and he saw him. That is His words: ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed nor erred, nor does he speak from desire﴾ ... to His words ﴿then he descended﴾: Jibril descended to Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿So he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The qab is half a finger." Some said: there was a distance of two cubits between them.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "He had six hundred wings," meaning Jibril, peace be upon him.

- Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Abu Usamah related to us, he said: Zakariyya related to us, from Ibn Ash'ath, from 'Amir, from Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: What is His words ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾? She said: That was Jibril; he used to come to him in the form of men, but he came to him this time in his true form, and he filled the horizon of the sky.

Others said: Rather, the one who drew near and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Jibril from his Lord.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "God, from Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the one who was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Muhammad from his Lord.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubayd al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: We said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you see your Lord?" He said: "I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice," then he recited ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾.

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr informed us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I was taken up, Jibril went on until he came to Paradise. He said: I entered and was given al-Kawthar. Then he went on until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and your Lord drew near and descended, so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: Allah revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed, taking His words ﴿what He revealed﴾ to mean the verbal noun (masdar).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "His servant Muhammad ﷺ, what his Lord revealed to him."

It may be directed under this interpretation that "ma" has two possibilities: one, that it means "alladhi" (that which), so the meaning of the speech would be "He revealed to His servant that which his Lord revealed to him." The other, that it means the verbal noun.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: al-Hasan said: "Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Upon the tongue of Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Jibril revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah revealed to him."

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: Jibril revealed to his servant Muhammad ﷺ what his Lord revealed to him, because the opening of the speech at the beginning of the surah proceeded with news about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and about Jibril, peace be upon him, and His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ are within that context, and nothing has come to indicate that the report has turned away from the two of them, so that it would be directed to something other than what it was directed to.

* *

As for His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The heart of Muhammad did not lie about what Muhammad saw, but affirmed it.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding what his heart saw without denying it. Some of them said: what his heart saw was the Lord of the worlds. They said: He placed his sight in his heart, so he saw Him with his heart and did not see Him with his eye.

Those who said that:

- Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, he said: My uncle Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id related to me, from Isra'il ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him with his heart ﷺ."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, he said: 'Abbad, meaning Ibn Mansur, informed us, he said: I asked 'Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. He said: Do you want me to say to you, "He saw Him, yes, he saw Him, then he saw Him, then he saw Him" until the breath runs out?

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah, and he was asked whether Muhammad saw his Lord. He said: Yes, he saw his Lord.

- He said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Salim, mawla of Mu'awiyah, related to us, from 'Ikrimah, the like of it.

- Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Tamimi related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn Sayyar related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Zurba, from 'Amr ibn Sulayman, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: O Muhammad, do you know about what the Exalted Assembly dispute? I said: No, my Lord. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what is in the heavens and the earth. I said: O my Lord, concerning the degrees, the expiations, the walking to the congregational prayers, and waiting for prayer after prayer. I said: O my Lord, You took Ibrahim as a close friend and spoke to Musa directly, and You did such and such? He said: Did I not expand your breast? Did I not remove your burden? Did I not do for you? Did I not do?" He said: "Then He communicated to me things that I was not permitted to narrate to you." He said: "That is His saying in His Book, which narrates it to you: ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed. The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾, so He placed the light of my sight in my heart, and I looked at Him with my heart."

- Muhammad ibn 'Imarah and Ahmad ibn Hisham related to me, they both said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him twice with his heart."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, from Qays, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah chose Ibrahim for intimate friendship, chose Musa for speech, and chose Muhammad for vision, peace be upon them.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ziyad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him with his heart."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from one who heard Ibn 'Abbas say regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: "Muhammad saw his Lord."

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie﴾, meaning he did not deny it, ﴿about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw his Lord."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart."

Others said: rather, what his heart saw and did not deny was Jibril, peace be upon him.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi related to me, he said: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, he said: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibril, upon whom were two green garments (rafraf) which filled what is between the heaven and the earth."

- Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril at Sidrat al-Muntaha, he had six hundred wings, shaking from his feathers pearls and rubies."

- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i and Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub related to us, they both said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, that al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to him, he said: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud related to me, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril at Sidrat al-Muntaha, he had six hundred wings." Al-Rifa'i added in his narration: I asked 'Asim about the wings, but he did not inform me, so I asked my companions, and they said: each wing is what lies between the east and the west.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Jibril in his true form, which is his form." He said: "And he is the one he saw descending another time."

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah, Makkah, Kufah and Basrah read ﴿kadhaba﴾ with light stress (takhfif), except 'Asim al-Jahdari, Abu Ja'far al-Qari' and al-Hasan al-Basri, who read it "kaddhaba" with heavy stress (tashdid), meaning: the heart did not lie about what it saw, but made it truth and certainty. It may also be possible, when read thus, that the meaning is: the possessor of the heart did not lie about what he saw. We have already explained the meaning of those who read it with light stress.

The recitation which, in my view, is the more correct of the two is the recitation of those who read it with light stress, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, while the other's soundness is not rejected, since its meaning is also sound.

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari related to us, he said: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "Jibril saw six hundred wings in his form."

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: Qabis ibn Layth al-Asadi related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril, peace be upon him, who had six hundred wings."

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The beginning of the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was that he saw Jibril in his dream at Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Jibril called out to him: "O Muhammad!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked right and left but saw nothing, three times. Then he went out and saw him, and he entered among the people, then went out again, or he said: then he looked, "I am unsure," and he saw him. That is His words: ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed nor erred, nor does he speak from desire﴾ ... to His words ﴿then he descended﴾: Jibril descended to Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿So he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The qab is half a finger." Some said: there was a distance of two cubits between them.

Others said: Rather, the one who drew near and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Jibril from his Lord.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "God, from Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the one who was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Muhammad from his Lord.

Those who said that:

He said: I entered and was given al-Kawthar. Then he went on until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and your Lord drew near and descended, so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: Allah revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed, taking His words ﴿what He revealed﴾ to mean the verbal noun (masdar).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "His servant Muhammad ﷺ, what his Lord revealed to him."

It may be directed under this interpretation that "ma" has two possibilities: one, that it means "alladhi" (that which), so the meaning of the speech would be "He revealed to His servant that which his Lord revealed to him." The other, that it means the verbal noun.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: al-Hasan said: "Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Upon the tongue of Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Jibril revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah revealed to him."

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: Jibril revealed to his servant Muhammad ﷺ what his Lord revealed to him, because the opening of the speech at the beginning of the surah proceeded with news about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and about Jibril, peace be upon him, and His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ are within that context, and nothing has come to indicate that the report has turned away from the two of them, so that it would be directed to something other than what it was directed to.

* *

As for His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The heart of Muhammad did not lie about what Muhammad saw, but affirmed it.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding what his heart saw without denying it. Some of them said: what his heart saw was the Lord of the worlds. They said: He placed his sight in his heart, so he saw Him with his heart and did not see Him with his eye.

Those who said that:

- Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, he said: My uncle Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id related to me, from Isra'il ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him with his heart ﷺ."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, he said: 'Abbad, meaning Ibn Mansur, informed us, he said: I asked 'Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. He said: Do you want me to say to you, "He saw Him, yes, he saw Him, then he saw Him, then he saw Him" until the breath runs out?

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah, and he was asked whether Muhammad saw his Lord. He said: Yes, he saw his Lord.

- He said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Salim, mawla of Mu'awiyah, related to us, from 'Ikrimah, the like of it.

- Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Tamimi related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn Sayyar related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Zurba, from 'Amr ibn Sulayman, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: O Muhammad, do you know about what the Exalted Assembly dispute? I said: No, my Lord. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what is in the heavens and the earth. I said: O my Lord, concerning the degrees, the expiations, the walking to the congregational prayers, and waiting for prayer after prayer. I said: O my Lord, You took Ibrahim as a close friend and spoke to Musa directly, and You did such and such? He said: Did I not expand your breast? Did I not remove your burden? Did I not do for you? Did I not do?" He said: "Then He communicated to me things that I was not permitted to narrate to you." He said: "That is His saying in His Book, which narrates it to you: ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed. The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾, so He placed the light of my sight in my heart, and I looked at Him with my heart."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, from Qays, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah chose Ibrahim for intimate friendship, chose Musa for speech, and chose Muhammad for vision, peace be upon them.

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from one who heard Ibn 'Abbas say regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: "Muhammad saw his Lord."

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie﴾, meaning he did not deny it, ﴿about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw his Lord."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart."

- Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril at Sidrat al-Muntaha, he had six hundred wings, shaking from his feathers pearls and rubies."

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. It may also be possible, when read thus, that the meaning is: the possessor of the heart did not lie about what he saw. We have already explained the meaning of those who read it with light stress.

The recitation which, in my view, is the more correct of the two is the recitation of those who read it with light stress, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, while the other's soundness is not rejected, since its meaning is also sound.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 8–11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾ [53:8], ﴿and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾ [53:9], ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ [53:10], ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾ [53:11].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then Jibril drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended to him. This is an example of the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) which is meant as the earlier: the meaning is "then he descended and drew near," but the mention of ﴿drew near﴾ first is fine, since drawing near indicates descending and descending indicates drawing near, as one says: "So-and-so visited me and did well [by me]," and "he did well to me and then visited me," and "he insulted me and then did harm," and "he did harm and then insulted me," because harm is insult and insult is harm.

The people of ta'wil (exegesis) said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "Jibril, peace be upon him."

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: meaning Jibril.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "It is Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: then the Lord drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended.

Those who said that:

- Yahya ibn al-Umawi related to us, he said: My father related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "His Lord drew near and descended."

- al-Rabi' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating to us about the night of the Isra' of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Jibril ascended with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the seventh heaven, then he rose with him to a place only Allah knows, until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and the Almighty, Lord of Might, drew near and descended, until there was between him and [Muhammad] two bow-lengths or closer. Then Allah revealed to him what He willed, and among what He revealed was fifty prayers upon his community every day and night," and he mentioned the hadith.

Did I not do?" He said: "Then He communicated to me things that I was not permitted to narrate to you." He said: "That is His saying in His Book, which narrates it to you: ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed. The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾, so He placed the light of my sight in my heart, and I looked at Him with my heart."

- Muhammad ibn 'Imarah and Ahmad ibn Hisham related to me, they both said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, he said: Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him twice with his heart."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, from Qays, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah chose Ibrahim for intimate friendship, chose Musa for speech, and chose Muhammad for vision, peace be upon them.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ziyad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him with his heart."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from one who heard Ibn 'Abbas say regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: "Muhammad saw his Lord."

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie﴾, meaning he did not deny it, ﴿about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw his Lord."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart."

Others said: rather, what his heart saw and did not deny was Jibril, peace be upon him.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bazi' al-Baghdadi related to me, he said: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, he said: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw Jibril, upon whom were two green garments (rafraf) which filled what is between the heaven and the earth."

- Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani related to us, he said: 'Amr ibn 'Asim related to us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril at Sidrat al-Muntaha, he had six hundred wings, shaking from his feathers pearls and rubies."

- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i and Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub related to us, they both said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab related to us, that al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to him, he said: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud related to me, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril at Sidrat al-Muntaha, he had six hundred wings." Al-Rifa'i added in his narration: I asked 'Asim about the wings, but he did not inform me, so I asked my companions, and they said: each wing is what lies between the east and the west.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Jibril in his true form, which is his form." He said: "And he is the one he saw descending another time."

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. The majority of the readers of Madinah, Makkah, Kufah and Basrah read ﴿kadhaba﴾ with light stress (takhfif), except 'Asim al-Jahdari, Abu Ja'far al-Qari' and al-Hasan al-Basri, who read it "kaddhaba" with heavy stress (tashdid), meaning: the heart did not lie about what it saw, but made it truth and certainty. It may also be possible, when read thus, that the meaning is: the possessor of the heart did not lie about what he saw. We have already explained the meaning of those who read it with light stress.

The recitation which, in my view, is the more correct of the two is the recitation of those who read it with light stress, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, while the other's soundness is not rejected, since its meaning is also sound.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 8–11:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾ [53:8], ﴿and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾ [53:9], ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ [53:10], ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾ [53:11].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then Jibril drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended to him. This is an example of the postponed (al-mu'akhkhar) which is meant as the earlier: the meaning is "then he descended and drew near," but the mention of ﴿drew near﴾ first is fine, since drawing near indicates descending and descending indicates drawing near, as one says: "So-and-so visited me and did well [by me]," and "he did well to me and then visited me," and "he insulted me and then did harm," and "he did harm and then insulted me," because harm is insult and insult is harm.

The people of ta'wil (exegesis) said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "Jibril, peace be upon him."

- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: meaning Jibril.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "It is Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: then the Lord drew near to Muhammad ﷺ and descended.

Those who said that:

- Yahya ibn al-Umawi related to us, he said: My father related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾: he said: "His Lord drew near and descended."

- al-Rabi' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrating to us about the night of the Isra' of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Jibril ascended with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the seventh heaven, then he rose with him to a place only Allah knows, until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and the Almighty, Lord of Might, drew near and descended, until there was between him and [Muhammad] two bow-lengths or closer. Then Allah revealed to him what He willed, and among what He revealed was fifty prayers upon his community every day and night," and he mentioned the hadith.

* *

As for His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾:

He says: So Jibril was from Muhammad ﷺ at the measure of two bow-lengths, or closer than that, meaning: nearer. It is said: "He is from him at a distance of qab qawsayn (two bow-lengths), qayb qawsayn, qid qawsayn, qad qawsayn, and qada qawsayn," all of which mean: the measure of two bows.

It was also said that the meaning of His words ﴿qab qawsayn﴾ is that he was at the place of the string on the bow.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "At the place of the string on the bow."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "Qid qawsayn" (the measure of two bows).

Qatadah said the same.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Khasif, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "Qid, or qadr (measure) of two bows."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from 'Asim, from Zirr, from 'Abd Allah regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "Jibril, peace be upon him, drew near to him until he was the measure of one or two cubits."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin regarding ﴿qab qawsayn﴾: he said: "It is not this bow, but the measure of two cubits or closer; and the qab is the qid."

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the referent of His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾. Some of them said, in accordance with what we have said regarding it:

- Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, he said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, he said: Zirr ibn Hubaysh related to us, he said: 'Abd Allah said regarding this verse ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw Jibril, he had six hundred wings."

- 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan al-Sukkari related to us, he said: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His words ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "Jibril saw six hundred wings in his form."

- Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: Qabis ibn Layth al-Asadi related to us, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The Prophet ﷺ saw Jibril, peace be upon him, who had six hundred wings."

- Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Ibn Lahi'ah related to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: The beginning of the matter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was that he saw Jibril in his dream at Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Jibril called out to him: "O Muhammad!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked right and left but saw nothing, three times. Then he went out and saw him, and he entered among the people, then went out again, or he said: then he looked, "I am unsure," and he saw him. That is His words: ﴿By the star when it sets, your companion has not strayed nor erred, nor does he speak from desire﴾ ... to His words ﴿then he descended﴾: Jibril descended to Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿So he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "The qab is half a finger." Some said: there was a distance of two cubits between them.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "He had six hundred wings," meaning Jibril, peace be upon him.

- Ibrahim ibn Sa'id related to us, he said: Abu Usamah related to us, he said: Zakariyya related to us, from Ibn Ash'ath, from 'Amir, from Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: What is His words ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾? She said: That was Jibril; he used to come to him in the form of men, but he came to him this time in his true form, and he filled the horizon of the sky.

Others said: Rather, the one who drew near and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Jibril from his Lord.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer﴾: he said: "God, from Jibril, peace be upon him."

Others said: Rather, the one who was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer was Muhammad from his Lord.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubayd al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: We said: "O Prophet of Allah, did you see your Lord?" He said: "I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice," then he recited ﴿Then he drew near and descended﴾.

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr informed us, he said: Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When I was taken up, Jibril went on until he came to Paradise. He said: I entered and was given al-Kawthar. Then he went on until he came to Sidrat al-Muntaha, and your Lord drew near and descended, so he was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed."

* *

As for His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾:

The people of ta'wil differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: Allah revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed, taking His words ﴿what He revealed﴾ to mean the verbal noun (masdar).

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "His servant Muhammad ﷺ, what his Lord revealed to him."

It may be directed under this interpretation that "ma" has two possibilities: one, that it means "alladhi" (that which), so the meaning of the speech would be "He revealed to His servant that which his Lord revealed to him." The other, that it means the verbal noun.

Those who said that:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: al-Hasan said: "Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Upon the tongue of Jibril."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', the like of it.

- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾: he said: "Jibril revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what Allah revealed to him."

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: Jibril revealed to his servant Muhammad ﷺ what his Lord revealed to him, because the opening of the speech at the beginning of the surah proceeded with news about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and about Jibril, peace be upon him, and His words ﴿and He revealed to His servant what He revealed﴾ are within that context, and nothing has come to indicate that the report has turned away from the two of them, so that it would be directed to something other than what it was directed to.

* *

As for His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The heart of Muhammad did not lie about what Muhammad saw, but affirmed it.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding what his heart saw without denying it. Some of them said: what his heart saw was the Lord of the worlds. They said: He placed his sight in his heart, so he saw Him with his heart and did not see Him with his eye.

Those who said that:

- Sa'id ibn Yahya related to us, he said: My uncle Sa'id 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id related to me, from Isra'il ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw Him with his heart ﷺ."

- Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, he said: 'Abbad, meaning Ibn Mansur, informed us, he said: I asked 'Ikrimah regarding His words: ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾. He said: Do you want me to say to you, "He saw Him, yes, he saw Him, then he saw Him, then he saw Him" until the breath runs out?

- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd related to us, he said: I heard 'Ikrimah, and he was asked whether Muhammad saw his Lord. He said: Yes, he saw his Lord.

- He said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Salim, mawla of Mu'awiyah, related to us, from 'Ikrimah, the like of it.

- Ahmad ibn 'Isa al-Tamimi related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn Sayyar related to us, he said: My father related to me, from Sa'id ibn Zurba, from 'Amr ibn Sulayman, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: O Muhammad, do you know about what the Exalted Assembly dispute? I said: No, my Lord. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I found its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what is in the heavens and the earth. I said: O my Lord, concerning the degrees, the expiations, the walking to the congregational prayers, and waiting for prayer after prayer. I said: O my Lord, You took Ibrahim as a close friend and spoke to Musa directly, and You did such and such? He said: Did I not expand your breast? Did I not remove your burden? Did I not do for you? Did I not do?" He said: "Then He communicated to me things that I was not permitted to narrate to you." He said: "That is His saying in His Book, which narrates it to you: ﴿Then he drew near and descended, and was at a distance of two bow-lengths or closer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed. The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾, so He placed the light of my sight in my heart, and I looked at Him with my heart."

- He said: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie﴾, meaning he did not deny it, ﴿about what it saw﴾: he said: "He saw his Lord."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' regarding ﴿The heart did not lie about what it saw﴾: he said: "Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart."

Others said: rather, what his heart saw and did not deny was Jibril, peace be upon him.

Those who said that:

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Will you then dispute with him over what he saw? (12) And he certainly saw him in another descent (13) at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (14) near it is the Garden of Refuge (15) when the Lote-tree was covered by that which covered it (16)﴾**

The readers (qurra') differed over the recitation (qira'ah) of ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and most of his companions recited it as "afatamrūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and without an alif, which is the recitation of most of the people of Kufa, and they interpreted it as "Will you deny it?"

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he used to recite "afatamrūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and without an alif, meaning: "Will you deny it?" As for the one who recited ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾, he said: "Will you dispute with him?" The majority of the readers of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' and with an alif, meaning: "Will you dispute with him?"

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations and both are sound in meaning, since the polytheists had denied that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen what Allah showed him on the night of his Night Journey (isrā'), and they disputed about it. So whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct.

The meaning of the statement is: "Will you, O polytheists, dispute with Muhammad about what he sees of the signs of Allah?"

* *

And His words ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نزلَةً أُخْرَى﴾ ("And he certainly saw him in another descent").

It means: he saw him once more.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the one whom Muhammad saw in another descent, in the same way they differed regarding His words: ﴿مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى﴾ ("The heart did not lie about what it saw").

Mention of some of what has been related about this difference:

Those who said that it was Jibril, peace be upon him:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, that 'Aisha said: "O Abu 'Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has committed a monstrous slander against Allah." He said: I had been reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, wait for me and do not hurry me. Tell me about the words of Allah: ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent, and he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾?" She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him once in his own form and shape in which he was created, and he saw him another time when he descended from the sky to the earth, his great form filling what is between the sky and the earth." She said: "I was the first of this Ummah to ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril, peace be upon him.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi and 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, with something similar.

⁕ Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I was with 'Aisha," and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said to him: "O Abu 'Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has committed a monstrous slander against Allah, and Allah says: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾ and ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾." He said: I had been reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, wait and do not hurry. Did not Allah say ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾?" She said: "I was the first of this Ummah to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: 'I did not see Jibril in his form except these two times, descending from the sky, his great form filling what is between the sky and the earth.'"

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I was reclining with 'Aisha, and she said: 'O Abu 'Aisha,'" and then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril in a rafraf (green silk cushion) that filled what is between the sky and the earth."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril with down on his feet like pearls, like drops of rain on herbage."

⁕ al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, regarding His words ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾, then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril in his form twice."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami, from Mujahid, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibril, peace be upon him, in his form twice."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "It is Jibril, peace be upon him."

⁕ 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Isma'il, from 'Amir, who said: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Ka'b, that he informed him that Allah, blessed and exalted, divided His vision and His speech between Musa and Muhammad. Musa was spoken to twice, and Muhammad saw Him twice." He said: "Masruq came to 'Aisha and said: 'O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad see his Lord?' She said: 'Glory be to Allah! My hair stood on end at what you said. Where are you from three things? Whoever tells you any of them has lied. Whoever tells you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied.' Then she recited ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision, and He is the Subtle, the Aware﴾ and ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾. 'Whoever tells you what will happen tomorrow has lied.' Then she recited the end of Surat Luqman: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾. 'Whoever tells you that Muhammad concealed anything of the revelation has lied.' Then she recited ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. She said: 'But he saw Jibril, peace be upon him, in his form twice.'"

⁕ Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to me, from 'Amir, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to us, saying: "I heard Ka'b," and then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan, except that in his version it says: "Muhammad saw Him once, and Musa was spoken to twice."

Mention of those who said: he saw his Lord, mighty and majestic.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw his Lord with his heart." A man then said to him: "Is it not that ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾?" 'Ikrimah said to him: "Do you not see the sky?" He said: "Yes." 'Ikrimah said: "Do you see all of it?"

⁕ Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent, at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾, that he said: "His Lord drew near and descended, and was at two bow-lengths or nearer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed." He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) had indeed seen him."

* *

And His words ﴿عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ ("at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary").

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "He certainly saw him at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." So "at" (ʿinda) is connected to His words ﴿saw him﴾. The sidrah is the nabq tree (jujube tree).

It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" according to the view of some scholars among the people of interpretation, because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said to him: 'Tell me about the words of Allah: (at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, near it is the Garden of Refuge).'" Ka'b said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne. The knowledge of every knower ends at it. It is a angel brought near, or a prophet sent. Beyond it is the unseen, which no one knows but Allah."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I was present. Ka'b said: 'It is a lote-tree on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of all creatures ends at it. No one has knowledge beyond it. That is why it was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, because knowledge ends at it.'"

Others said: It was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because whatever descends from above it and whatever ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, from 'Adi, from Talhah al-Yami, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he was brought to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, which is in the sixth heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth or from below it ends at it, and it is taken from there, and whatever descends from above it ends at it, and it is received there."

⁕ Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Ya'la narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: "I said to al-Dahhak: 'Why is it called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary?' He said: 'Because every matter from the command of Allah ends at it and does not go beyond it.'"

Others said: It was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because everyone who followed the Sunnah and the path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' (at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary), who said: "Everyone ends at it except those who follow the Sunnah of Ahmad (ﷺ), and for that reason it was called the Utmost Boundary."

⁕ 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Abu Hurayrah, or someone else (Abu Ja'far al-Razi was uncertain): "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: 'This is the Lote-tree to which everyone ends except those of your Ummah who follow your Sunnah.'"

The correct view on this is to say that the meaning of "al-Muntaha" is "the end," so it is as if it were said: "at the Lote-tree of the end." It is permissible that it was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because the knowledge of every knowing creature ends at it, as Ka'b said. It is permissible that it was so called because whatever ascends from below it and descends from above it ends at it, as was narrated from 'Abd Allah. It is permissible that it was so called because everyone among the people who followed the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ends at it. And it is permissible that it was so called for all of that, and there is no report that conclusively settles that it was called so for some of these reasons and not others. So there is no view more sound regarding it than the view our Lord, may His majesty be exalted, stated, which is that it is the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary.

It is by what we have said, that it is the nabq tree, that reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the statements of the scholars have been transmitted in succession.

Mention of what has been related about that, and the statements of the scholars:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and its nabq was like jars, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it transformed into rubies, emeralds and the like."

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I reached the seventh heaven, I came upon Ibrahim, and I said: 'O Jibril, who is this?' He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim.' I greeted him, and he said: 'Welcome, the righteous son and the righteous prophet.' Then the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and the Prophet of Allah described that its nabq was like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn 'Anbasah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I rode the Buraq, then I was taken to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. Its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and its fruit was like jars. When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it changed, and no one can describe its beauty. Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed."
