- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: He said: The dwellings of the martyrs.

* *

And His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And he certainly saw Him in another descent, when there covers the Lote Tree that which covers. So ﴿when﴾ (idh) is connected to ﴿he saw﴾.

The interpreters differed regarding what covers the Lote Tree. Some of them said: What covered it was a swarm of gold (farash al-dhahab).

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, on the authority of Talhah al-Yami, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of 'Abdullah, regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Muslim or Talhah ("al-A'mash was uncertain"), on the authority of Masruq, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw it with my own eyes, the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, until I was certain of it; then a swarm of gold came between me and it."
- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw it until I was certain of it, then a swarm of gold came between me and it."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Musa, meaning Ibn 'Ubaydah, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Zayd, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: What did you see that covered the Lote Tree? He said: I saw it covered by a swarm of gold."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, what did you see covering that lote tree? He said: I saw it covered by a swarm of gold, and I saw upon every leaf of its leaves an angel standing, glorifying Allah.

Others said: What covered it was the Lord of Might and His angels.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: Allah covered it, and Muhammad saw of the Greatest Signs of his Lord.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The branches of the Lote Tree were pearls, rubies or chrysolite, and Muhammad saw it, and Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi', regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The light of the Lord covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight upon a tree.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi', with similar wording.
- 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or another ("Abu Ja'far was uncertain"), who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree, and the light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they alight upon a tree. He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment, and said to him: Ask.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Will you then dispute with him over what he saw? (12) And he certainly saw him in another descent (13) at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (14) near it is the Garden of Refuge (15) when the Lote-tree was covered by that which covered it (16)﴾**

The readers (qurra') differed over the recitation (qira'ah) of ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾. Ibn Mas'ud and most of his companions recited it as "afatamrūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and without an alif, which is the recitation of most of the people of Kufa, and they interpreted it as "Will you deny it?"

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he used to recite "afatamrūnahu" with a fatḥah on the tā' and without an alif, meaning: "Will you deny it?" As for the one who recited ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾, he said: "Will you dispute with him?" The majority of the readers of Medina, Mecca and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ﴾ with a ḍammah on the tā' and with an alif, meaning: "Will you dispute with him?"

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations and both are sound in meaning, since the polytheists had denied that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had seen what Allah showed him on the night of his Night Journey (isrā'), and they disputed about it. So whichever of the two a reader recites, he is correct.

The meaning of the statement is: "Will you, O polytheists, dispute with Muhammad about what he sees of the signs of Allah?"

* *

And His words ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نزلَةً أُخْرَى﴾ ("And he certainly saw him in another descent").

It means: he saw him once more.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the one whom Muhammad saw in another descent, in the same way they differed regarding His words: ﴿مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَى﴾ ("The heart did not lie about what it saw").

Mention of some of what has been related about this difference:

Those who said that it was Jibril, peace be upon him:

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, that 'Aisha said: "O Abu 'Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has committed a monstrous slander against Allah." He said: I had been reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, wait for me and do not hurry me. Tell me about the words of Allah: ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent, and he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾?" She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him once in his own form and shape in which he was created, and he saw him another time when he descended from the sky to the earth, his great form filling what is between the sky and the earth." She said: "I was the first of this Ummah to ask the Prophet (ﷺ) about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril, peace be upon him.'"

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi and 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, with something similar.

⁕ Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I was with 'Aisha," and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said to him: "O Abu 'Aisha, whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has committed a monstrous slander against Allah, and Allah says: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾ and ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾." He said: I had been reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, wait and do not hurry. Did not Allah say ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾?" She said: "I was the first of this Ummah to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that, and he said: 'I did not see Jibril in his form except these two times, descending from the sky, his great form filling what is between the sky and the earth.'"

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I was reclining with 'Aisha, and she said: 'O Abu 'Aisha,'" and then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril in a rafraf (green silk cushion) that filled what is between the sky and the earth."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril with down on his feet like pearls, like drops of rain on herbage."

⁕ al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Murrah, regarding His words ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾, then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "He saw Jibril in his form twice."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami, from Mujahid, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) saw Jibril, peace be upon him, in his form twice."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "It is Jibril, peace be upon him."

⁕ 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Isma'il, from 'Amir, who said: "'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to me, from Ka'b, that he informed him that Allah, blessed and exalted, divided His vision and His speech between Musa and Muhammad. Musa was spoken to twice, and Muhammad saw Him twice." He said: "Masruq came to 'Aisha and said: 'O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad see his Lord?' She said: 'Glory be to Allah! My hair stood on end at what you said. Where are you from three things? Whoever tells you any of them has lied. Whoever tells you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied.' Then she recited ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision, and He is the Subtle, the Aware﴾ and ﴿It is not for any human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil﴾. 'Whoever tells you what will happen tomorrow has lied.' Then she recited the end of Surat Luqman: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die﴾. 'Whoever tells you that Muhammad concealed anything of the revelation has lied.' Then she recited ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. She said: 'But he saw Jibril, peace be upon him, in his form twice.'"

⁕ Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Isma'il narrated to me, from 'Amir, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal narrated to us, saying: "I heard Ka'b," and then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan, except that in his version it says: "Muhammad saw Him once, and Musa was spoken to twice."

Mention of those who said: he saw his Lord, mighty and majestic.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent﴾: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw his Lord with his heart." A man then said to him: "Is it not that ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾?" 'Ikrimah said to him: "Do you not see the sky?" He said: "Yes." 'Ikrimah said: "Do you see all of it?"

⁕ Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's words ﴿And he certainly saw him in another descent, at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾, that he said: "His Lord drew near and descended, and was at two bow-lengths or nearer, and He revealed to His servant what He revealed." He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) had indeed seen him."

* *

And His words ﴿عِنْدَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنْتَهَى﴾ ("at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary").

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "He certainly saw him at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." So "at" (ʿinda) is connected to His words ﴿saw him﴾. The sidrah is the nabq tree (jujube tree).

It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" according to the view of some scholars among the people of interpretation, because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said to him: 'Tell me about the words of Allah: (at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, near it is the Garden of Refuge).'" Ka'b said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne. The knowledge of every knower ends at it. It is a angel brought near, or a prophet sent. Beyond it is the unseen, which no one knows but Allah."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me, from al-A'mash, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, who said: "Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and I was present. Ka'b said: 'It is a lote-tree on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of all creatures ends at it. No one has knowledge beyond it. That is why it was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, because knowledge ends at it.'"

Others said: It was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because whatever descends from above it and whatever ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, from 'Adi, from Talhah al-Yami, from Murrah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he was brought to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, which is in the sixth heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth or from below it ends at it, and it is taken from there, and whatever descends from above it ends at it, and it is received there."

⁕ Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi narrated to me, saying: Ya'la narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: "I said to al-Dahhak: 'Why is it called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary?' He said: 'Because every matter from the command of Allah ends at it and does not go beyond it.'"

Others said: It was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because everyone who followed the Sunnah and the path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ends at it.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' (at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary), who said: "Everyone ends at it except those who follow the Sunnah of Ahmad (ﷺ), and for that reason it was called the Utmost Boundary."

⁕ 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Abu Hurayrah, or someone else (Abu Ja'far al-Razi was uncertain): "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: 'This is the Lote-tree to which everyone ends except those of your Ummah who follow your Sunnah.'"

The correct view on this is to say that the meaning of "al-Muntaha" is "the end," so it is as if it were said: "at the Lote-tree of the end." It is permissible that it was called the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary because the knowledge of every knowing creature ends at it, as Ka'b said. It is permissible that it was so called because whatever ascends from below it and descends from above it ends at it, as was narrated from 'Abd Allah. It is permissible that it was so called because everyone among the people who followed the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ends at it. And it is permissible that it was so called for all of that, and there is no report that conclusively settles that it was called so for some of these reasons and not others. So there is no view more sound regarding it than the view our Lord, may His majesty be exalted, stated, which is that it is the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary.

It is by what we have said, that it is the nabq tree, that reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the statements of the scholars have been transmitted in succession.

Mention of what has been related about that, and the statements of the scholars:

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and its nabq was like jars, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants. When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it transformed into rubies, emeralds and the like."

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When I reached the seventh heaven, I came upon Ibrahim, and I said: 'O Jibril, who is this?' He said: 'This is your father Ibrahim.' I greeted him, and he said: 'Welcome, the righteous son and the righteous prophet.' Then the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and the Prophet of Allah described that its nabq was like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna also narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with something similar.

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned something similar.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn 'Anbasah narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I rode the Buraq, then I was taken to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. Its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and its fruit was like jars. When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it changed, and no one can describe its beauty. Then Allah revealed to me what He revealed."

⁕ Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The angel ascended with me," and he said: "Then I reached the Lote-tree, and I knew that it was a lote-tree; I knew its leaves and its fruit." He said: "When there covered it what covered it by the command of Allah, it changed until no one can describe it."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), similar to that, except that he said: "until I cannot describe it."

⁕ 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Abu Hurayrah, or someone else (Abu Ja'far al-Razi was uncertain), who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: 'This is the Lote-tree to which everyone ends except those of your Ummah who follow your Sunnah. Behold, it is a tree from whose root rivers of water that is not stagnant flow, and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey. It is a tree under whose shade a rider walks for seventy years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole Ummah.'"

⁕ And Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl al-Hadrami, from al-Hasan al-'Urani, whom I think narrated from al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary," who said: "Among the fruits of Paradise upon it or upon him is an abundance of green silk and brocade, or an abundance was placed upon it."

⁕ And Ibn Humayd narrated to us again, from Mihran, who said: from al-Hasan al-'Urani, from al-Hudhayl, from Ibn Mas'ud, "and he did not doubt it," and he added in it: he said: "Sabr al-Jannah" means its middle; and he also said: "Upon it are abundant green silk and brocade."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from al-Hasan al-'Urani, from al-Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary," who said: "Sabr al-Jannah, upon it is green silk and brocade."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said: 'A hundred riders can travel in the shade of its branch,' or he said: 'A hundred riders can rest in the shade of its branches.' (Yahya was uncertain.) 'Upon it are golden butterflies, and its fruit is like jars.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', regarding the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, who said: "The lote-tree is a tree under whose shade a rider walks for a hundred years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole Ummah."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿at the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary﴾, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Lote-tree of its end was raised for me in the seventh heaven. Its nabq is like the jars of Hajar, and its leaves are like the ears of elephants. From its trunk flow two apparent rivers and two hidden rivers." He said: "I said to Jibril: 'What are these two rivers?'" [[In the manuscript no. 100, Tafsir, Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyyah (vol. 22: 59b), the word may be distorted, or it may be an addition by the copyist's pen.]] He said: "As for the two hidden rivers, they are in Paradise, and as for the two apparent rivers, they are the Nile and the Euphrates."

*

And His saying: ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Near the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary is the Garden of Refuge, the abode of the martyrs.

The interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: He said: It is the right side of the Throne, and it is the dwelling of the martyrs.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: He said: It is like His saying ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge, as an abode for what they used to do﴾.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Ma'mar, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Near it is the Garden of Refuge﴾: He said: The dwellings of the martyrs.

* *

And His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And he certainly saw Him in another descent, when there covers the Lote Tree that which covers. So ﴿when﴾ (idh) is connected to ﴿he saw﴾.

The interpreters differed regarding what covers the Lote Tree. Some of them said: What covered it was a swarm of gold (farash al-dhahab).

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Umarah narrated to me, saying: Sahl ibn 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi, on the authority of Talhah al-Yami, on the authority of Murrah, on the authority of 'Abdullah, regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Muslim or Talhah ("al-A'mash was uncertain"), on the authority of Masruq, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw it with my own eyes, the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary, until I was certain of it; then a swarm of gold came between me and it."
- Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I saw it until I was certain of it, then a swarm of gold came between me and it."
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibrahim, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: A swarm of gold covered it.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Musa, meaning Ibn 'Ubaydah, on the authority of Ya'qub ibn Zayd, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked: What did you see that covered the Lote Tree? He said: I saw it covered by a swarm of gold."
- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, what did you see covering that lote tree? He said: I saw it covered by a swarm of gold, and I saw upon every leaf of its leaves an angel standing, glorifying Allah.

Others said: What covered it was the Lord of Might and His angels.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: Allah covered it, and Muhammad saw of the Greatest Signs of his Lord.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The branches of the Lote Tree were pearls, rubies or chrysolite, and Muhammad saw it, and Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi', regarding ﴿When there covers the Lote Tree that which covers﴾: He said: The light of the Lord covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight upon a tree.
- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ja'far, on the authority of al-Rabi', with similar wording.
- 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to us, on the authority of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-'Aliyah al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or another ("Abu Ja'far was uncertain"), who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree, and the light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they alight upon a tree. He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment, and said to him: Ask.

The Exegesis of the Verse: Allah the Exalted says, ﴿His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾ (53:17) and ﴿He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾ (53:18).

Allah the Exalted says: The sight of Muhammad (ﷺ) did not incline to the right or the left away from what he saw, meaning he did not exceed what he was commanded to do, and he did not go beyond the limit set for him.

What we have said about this is also what the people of ta'wil (the interpreters of the Qur'an, sing. mufassir, one who engages in tafsir, i.e. exegesis) have said.

Those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾. He said: It did not swerve to the right or the left, nor did it transgress, nor go beyond what he was commanded.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, regarding ﴿His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾. He said: He saw Gabriel in the form of an angel.

[He] said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Muslim al-Batin, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress﴾. He said: "Did not swerve" means it did not go to the right or the left; "did not transgress" means it did not go beyond.

* *

As for His words ﴿He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾:

Allah the Exalted says: Muhammad certainly saw there some of the greatest signs and proofs of his Lord.

The people of ta'wil differed regarding those greatest signs. Some of them said: He saw a green rafraf (a cushion or carpet of green silk) that filled the horizon.

Those who said this:

Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqama, from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud), regarding ﴿He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾. He said: A green rafraf from Paradise that filled the horizon.

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said, and mentioned the like of it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqama, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding ﴿of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾. He said: A green rafraf that filled the horizon.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from al-A'mash, that Ibn Mas'ud said: The Prophet (ﷺ) saw a green rafraf from Paradise that filled the horizon.

Others said: He saw Gabriel in his (true) form.

Those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord﴾: Gabriel was seen by him in his creation through which he exists in the heavens, at a distance of two bow-lengths from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), between him and him.

On the interpretation of His saying: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, would be an unfair division."

His saying, exalted is He, means: Have you considered, O polytheists, al-Lat, which was formed from Allah with the letter ta' added to make it feminine, just as 'Amr was said for the male and 'Amra for the female, and as 'Abbas was said for the male and then 'Abbasa for the female. In the same way, the polytheists named their idols with names derived from the name of Allah, may He be mentioned and exalted, so they said: from Allah, al-Lat; and from al-'Aziz, al-'Uzza. They claimed that these goddesses were daughters of Allah. Exalted is Allah above what they say, and they have invented lies. So His majesty said to them: Have you considered, O you who claim that al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, are daughters of Allah, "Is the male for you" – meaning: Do you choose for yourselves the male among children and dislike the female for Him, and attribute to Him "the female" which you do not accept for yourselves? Rather, you bury her alive out of your aversion to them.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying "al-Lat". The majority of the readers of the principal cities read it with a light (unshaddated) ta', according to the meaning I have described. It is mentioned that al-Lat was a house in Nakhla which Quraysh worshipped. Others said it was in al-Ta'if.

Those who said so:

In accordance with what we have said concerning the interpretation of His saying "qisma dhizā", the people of interpretation said – though their expressions differed in describing it – some said: a crooked division.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "tilka idhan qisma dhizā": he said: crooked.

Others said: an unjust division.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding "tilka idhan qisma dhizā": he says: an unjust division.

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding "qisma dhizā": he said: an unjust division.

- Muhammad ibn Hafs Abu 'Ubayd al-Wasa'i [I have not found him in al-Khulasa, nor in al-Taj, and I do not know to what he is attributed] related to us, who said: Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ibn Lahi'a related to us, from Ibn 'Amra, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying "tilka idhan qisma dhizā": he said: that is then an unjust division with no right in it.

Others said: a deficient division.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, regarding "tilka idhan qisma dhizā": he said: deficient.

Others said: a contrary division.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "tilka idhan qisma dhizā": he said: they assigned daughters to Allah, blessed and exalted, and they assigned the angels as daughters of Allah, and worshipped them; and he recited "Has He taken daughters from what He creates and chosen sons for you? And when one of them is given good news..." to the end of the verse; and he recited "And they assign to Allah daughters..." to the end of the verse; and he said: they claimed for Allah a child, as the Jews and Christians did. And he recited "Thus said those before them" and said: "dhizā" in the speech of the Arabs means contrary. And he recited "They are only names which you and your fathers have named..."

On the interpretation of His saying: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, would be an unfair division."

His saying, exalted is He, means: Have you considered, O polytheists, al-Lat, which was formed from Allah with the letter ta' added to make it feminine, just as 'Amr was said for the male and 'Amra for the female, and as 'Abbas was said for the male and then 'Abbasa for the female. In the same way, the polytheists named their idols with names derived from the name of Allah, may He be mentioned and exalted, so they said: from Allah, al-Lat; and from al-'Aziz, al-'Uzza. They claimed that these goddesses were daughters of Allah. Exalted is Allah above what they say, and they have invented lies. So His majesty said to them: Have you considered, O you who claim that al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, the third, are daughters of Allah, "Is the male for you" – meaning: Do you choose for yourselves the male among children and dislike the female for Him, and attribute to Him "the female" which you do not accept for yourselves? Rather, you bury her alive out of your aversion to them.

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying "al-Lat". The majority of the readers of the principal cities read it with a light (unshaddated) ta', according to the meaning I have described. It is mentioned that al-Lat was a house in Nakhla which Quraysh worshipped. Others said it was in al-Ta'if.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding "Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza": as for al-Lat, it was at al-Ta'if.

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza": he said: al-Lat was a house in Nakhla which Quraysh worshipped.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Abu Salih read it "al-Latt" with a shaddah on the ta', and they took it as an attribute of the idol they worshipped, and said: he was a man who kneaded sawiq (a porridge of parched grain) for the pilgrims; when he died they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped him.

Those who related this report from them:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding "Have you considered al-Latt and al-'Uzza": he said: he used to knead sawiq for the pilgrims, so they devoted themselves to his grave.

- He said: Mu'ammal related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding "Have you considered al-Latt": he said: al-Lat: he used to knead sawiq for the pilgrims.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding "al-Latt": he said: he used to knead sawiq, then died, so they devoted themselves to his grave.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying "al-Latt": he said: a man who kneaded sawiq for the polytheists; he died, so they devoted themselves to his grave.

- Ahmad ibn Hisham related to us, who said: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying "al-Latt": he said: al-Latt: the one who would attend to their gods, kneading sawiq for them, and it was at al-Ta'if.

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf related to me, who said: Abu 'Ubayd related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, from Abu al-Ashhab, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: he used to knead sawiq for the pilgrims.

The reading most correct in our view is the reading of the one who reads it with a light ta', according to the meaning I have described for its reader, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers of the principal cities upon it.

As for al-'Uzza, the people of interpretation differed concerning it. Some said: it was trees they worshipped.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: Mu'ammal related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding "and al-'Uzza": he said: al-'Uzza: small trees.

Others said: al-'Uzza was a white stone.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said regarding "al-'Uzza": a white stone.

Others said: it was a house in al-Ta'if worshipped by Thaqif.

Those who said so:

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "and al-'Uzza": he said: al-'Uzza: a house in al-Ta'if worshipped by Thaqif.

Others said: rather, it was in the valley of Nakhla.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding "and Manat, the third, the other": he said: as for Manat, it was at Qudayd, a deity they worshipped, meaning al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat.

- Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying "and Manat, the third, the other": he said: Manat was a house at al-Mushallal which the Banu Ka'b worshipped.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verse 23:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿These are but names which you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority concerning them. They follow but conjecture and what their souls desire. And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: These names that you have named, namely al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other, are only names that you, O polytheists who associate others with Allah, and your fathers before you, have named. Allah has not sent down any authority for them, meaning for these names; that is, He has not permitted you to do that, nor has He authorised you to do it.

As:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿authority﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

* *

As for His saying ﴿They follow but conjecture﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: These polytheists follow, concerning these names with which they named their deities, nothing but conjecture, the assumption that what they say is true, not certainty. ﴿And what their souls desire﴾ means: and the desire of their souls, because they did not take this from a revelation that came to them from Allah, nor from a messenger of Allah who informed them of it. Rather, they invented it from themselves, or they took it from their fathers, who were upon the same disbelief in Allah as they were.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord﴾

He says: There has already come to these polytheists who associate others with Allah, from their Lord, the clarification, concerning that in which they are without certainty, namely their naming al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat the third with these names and their worship of them. He says: Guidance has come to them from their Lord concerning that, and clarification through the revelation which We revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), that worshipping them is not fitting, and that worship is suitable only for Allah, the One, the Subduer.

Ibn Zayd said concerning this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord﴾ "But they did not benefit from it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 24–26:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes? (24) But to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first life. (25) And how many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all, except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves.﴾ (26)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Or did Muhammad (ﷺ) desire what Allah had bestowed upon him of this honour with which He had honoured him, namely prophethood and messengership, and the revelation sent down to him, and wish for that, and his Lord granted it to him? To Allah belongs what is in the Hereafter and the first (i.e., this world, the Dunya). He gives to whom He wills of His creation what He wills, and withholds from whom He wills among them what He wills.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Or does man have whatever he wishes?﴾: "Even if Muhammad wished for this, it is his."

And His saying ﴿And how many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: And how many an angel there is in the heavens: many of the angels of Allah, whose intercession with Allah will not benefit at all those for whom they intercede, except that they intercede for him after Allah gives them permission to intercede for whom He wills of them, and approves, meaning: after He approves of His angels who intercede for someone, that they should intercede for him; then their intercession will benefit him at that time. This is only a rebuke from Allah, the Exalted, to the idol-worshippers, the chiefs of Quraysh and others who used to say ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in closeness﴾. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said to them: The intercession of My angels, who are in My presence, does not benefit those for whom they intercede except after My permission to them to intercede for him and My approval; so how about the intercession of those other than them? Thus He informed them that the intercession of what they worship besides Him will not benefit them.

His saying, dhikruhu (exalted is His remembrance), means: Indeed those who do not affirm the resurrection in the Hereafter, which is the Day of Resurrection, name the angels of Allah with the names of females. That is because they used to say: they are the daughters of Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said, in agreement with what we have said regarding His saying ﴿the naming of females﴾:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, he said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the naming of females﴾, he said: "the females."

* *

He, exalted is He, says: and what do they have of true knowledge in their saying, in naming the angels with the names of females? ﴿They follow only assumption﴾: he says, they follow in that nothing but assumption; meaning, they only say that out of assumption, without knowledge.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And indeed assumption avails not against the truth at all﴾

He says: indeed assumption does not benefit at all against the truth, such that it could take its place.

As for His saying ﴿So turn away from one who turns away from Our remembrance﴾, He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): so leave alone, O Muhammad, the one who turns his back on the remembrance of Allah and does not believe in Him, so that He may be made One.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and desires none but the worldly life﴾

He says: and he does not seek what is with Allah in the Hereafter, but rather seeks the adornment of the worldly life and aspires to remain in it.
