**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 53, verses 31–32 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best (reward)﴾ [53:31] ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults (lamam)﴾ [53:32].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿To Allah belongs﴾ the dominion over ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of anything. ﴿He leads astray whom He wills, and He knows best about them.﴾ ﴿So that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did﴾: meaning, so that He may recompense those among His creatures who disobeyed Him, who did evil by their disobedience toward Him, by requiting them with the Fire. ﴿And recompense those who did good with the best﴾: meaning, and so that He may recompense those who obeyed Him and did good by their obedience toward Him in this world, with the best (reward), which is Paradise, by rewarding them with it.

It has been said: this refers to the people of polytheism and the people of faith.

Those who said this:
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿so that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good﴾: "They are the believers."

* *

As for His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins﴾:
That is: those who keep far from the major sins which Allah has forbidden and made unlawful for them, so that they do not approach them. These include associating partners with Allah, and what we have already explained in His words ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove your evil deeds from you﴾ [4:31].

* *

As for His words ﴿and the immoralities﴾:
These are adultery and what is similar to it, for which Allah has prescribed a legal punishment (hadd).

* *

As for His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾:
The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "illa" (except) in this place. Some of them said: it carries the sense of the disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes). They said: the meaning of the statement is: "those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for the minor faults that they committed in the immoral acts and immoralities during the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) before Islam, for Allah has pardoned them for that and will not hold them to account for it."

Those who said this:
• ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: he said, "except what has already passed."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The polytheists used to do these things in the past, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿except for minor faults﴾, meaning what they did during the Age of Ignorance." He said: "And the minor faults (lamam) are what they committed of those major sins and immoralities in the Age of Ignorance before Islam, and He forgave them when they embraced Islam."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAyyash, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muhammad, who said: A man asked Zayd ibn Thabit about this verse, ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "Allah has forbidden you immoralities, whether apparent or hidden."
• Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The major sins of polytheism and the immoralities of adultery. They abandoned that when they entered Islam, so Allah forgave them what they had committed of it and done of it before Islam."

Some scholars of the Arabic language, who direct the interpretation of "illa" in this place to this aspect that I have mentioned from Ibn Abbas, said in explaining it: "It is not permitted for them to commit minor faults, and it is neither among the immoralities nor among the major sins. An exception may be made of a thing from another thing, though it is not part of it, on the basis of an implied reference to something from which one has refrained. Its meaning is: except that a person may commit something that is neither immorality nor a major sin." He said, quoting the poet:

*And a land in which there is no companion, except the yaʿafir (gazelles) and except the ʿis (camels)*

[[The verse is one of the examples cited by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Quran (folio 231), who said, regarding the words of Allah (those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities except for minor faults): "It is not permitted for them to commit minor faults, and it is neither among the immoralities nor among the major sins. An exception may be made of a thing from another thing, though it is not part of it, on the basis of an implied reference to something from which one has refrained. Its meaning: except that a person may commit something which is neither among the immoralities nor the major sins." He said: "And a land in which there is no companion… the two verses." Yaʿafir means gazelles, and ʿis means camels; neither of them is human, so it is as if he said: there is no companion in it, except that there are gazelles and camels in it. Some said: the yaʿfur among gazelles is the red one, and the aʿyas is the white gazelle. End quote. Al-Ayni said in Fara'id al-qala'id: it was said by Jiran al-Awd al-Numayri, whose name is Amir ibn al-Harith. The point of evidence is in "illa al-yaʿafir," since it is an exception from the word "companion" by substitution (badal), even though it is disjunctive, according to the dialect of the Banu Tamim, whereas the people of the Hijaz require the accusative case (for disjunctive exceptions). Yaʿafir is the plural of yaʿfur, which is the young of the wild cow, and ʿis is the plural of ʿaysa', which are white camels whose whiteness is mixed with some reddish tint. End quote. Al-Farra said in Maʿani al-Quran (folio 316), regarding His words "except for minor faults": "It means: except what is close to small sins." He said: "I heard from some Arabs: alamma yafʿalu (he almost did), in the sense of kada yafʿalu (he was about to do)." Al-Kalbi mentioned with his chain that it is a glance without deliberate intent, so it is a minor fault (lamam) and is forgiven; but if he repeats the glance, it is no longer a minor fault, it is a sin. End quote.]]

The yaʿafir are gazelles, and the ʿis are camels, and they are not people; so it is as if he said: there is no companion in it, but there are gazelles and camels in it. Some said: the yaʿfur among gazelles is the red one, and the aʿyas is the white one.

Many exegetes said something similar to this view.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, that Ibn Masʿud said: "The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the lips is kissing, the adultery of the hands is seizing, and the adultery of the feet is walking. The private part confirms this or denies it. If one advances with his private part, he is an adulterer; otherwise it is a minor fault (lamam)."
• Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have not seen anything more similar to the minor fault than what Abu Hurayra said from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Allah has written for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which will inevitably befall him. The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speech, the soul desires and longs, and the private part confirms this or denies it.'"
• Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Muawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masruq, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "If it precedes, it is adultery; if it follows, it is a minor fault."
• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Shaʿbi about the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is what falls short of adultery." Then he mentioned to us from Ibn Masʿud, who said: "The adultery of the eyes is what they look at; the adultery of the hand is what it touches; the adultery of the foot is where it walks; and the actual fulfilment is with the private part."
• Muhammad ibn Maʿmar related to me, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym ibn Amr al-Qari narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafiʿ, who is called Ibn Lubaba al-Taʾifi, narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu Hurayra about the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is the kiss, the squeeze, the glance, and the intimate contact; when the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, the ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory, and that is adultery."

Others said: rather, this is a genuine exception (istithna' muttasil, an exception of the same category), and the meaning of the statement is: "those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults, unless one commits them and then repents."

Those who said this:
• Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is the man who commits an immorality and then repents." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

*"If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive much, and which of Your servants is there who has not committed a fault?"*

[[The verse is by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt (Lisan al-Arab: lamm). He said: "al-ilmam and al-lamm: approaching a sin. It was also said: lamm is what is less than the major sins. In the revealed Book: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾." Alam al-rajul, from lamm, means small sins. Umayya said: "If You forgive, O Allah… the two verses." It is said: it is approaching disobedience without actually committing it. Al-Akhfash said: lamm is approaching sins. Ibn Barri said: the poem belongs to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt. He said: Abd al-Rahman (nephew of al-Asmaʿi) mentioned, from his uncle, from Yaʿqub (Ibn al-Sikkit), from Muslim ibn Abi Tarafa al-Hudhali, who said: Abu Khirash (the Hudhali poet) passed by, running between al-Safa and al-Marwa, saying:

*O God, this is the fifth, if he should complete it: may God complete it, and he has completed it.*
*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*]]

• Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "It is the one who commits a sin and then leaves it." And the poet said:

*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*

• Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buzayʿ related to me, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayra, I think he traced it to the Prophet: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "The lamma (slight lapse) of adultery, then he repents and does not return; the lamma of theft, then he repents and does not return; the lamma of drinking wine, then he repents and does not return." He said: "That is the ilmam."
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "A lamma of adultery or theft or drinking wine, then he does not return."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "A lamma of adultery, or theft, or drinking wine, then he does not return."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: this man commits a lamma of adultery, or a lamma of drinking wine, then he hides it and repents from it."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "except for minor faults": "One who commits it at the moment; I said: adultery? He said: adultery, then he repents."
• Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar said: "al-Hasan used to say about the lamm: a man commits a lapse of immorality, then he repents."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, who said: "Adultery, then he repents."
• [Ibn Humayd] said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, concerning "except for minor faults": "That he falls into a fall and then desists."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The lamam is one who commits it once."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Amr ibn Shuʿayb, that Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: "The lamam is what is less than polytheism."
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Murra narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "A lapse that one commits of sins."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "The man who commits a sin and then turns away from it." He said: "The people of the Age of Ignorance used to circumambulate the House saying:

*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*"

Others said, among those who directed the meaning of "illa" to the disjunctive exception: the lamam is what falls short of the worldly limit and the limit of the Hereafter, which Allah has pardoned.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ata, from Ibn al-Zubayr, concerning "except for minor faults": "It is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter."
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "The lamam is what falls short of the two limits: the limit of this world and the Hereafter."
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam and Qatada, from Ibn Abbas, with the like of this, except that he said: "The limit of this world, and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba informed us, from al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The lamam is what falls short of the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter, is expiated by the prayers, and it is the lamam, and it is less than every prescribed penalty. As for the limit of this world, it is every punishment which Allah has ordained to be inflicted in this world; and as for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything for which Allah has decreed the Fire and deferred its punishment to the Hereafter."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "It means: what lies between the two limits; every sin for which there is no prescribed penalty in this world nor punishment in the Hereafter is the lamam."
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The lamam is what lies between the two limits, which does not reach the limit of this world nor the limit that entails the Hereafter, for which Allah has made the Fire obligatory for its people, or an immorality for which the prescribed penalty is inflicted in this world."
• Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from Qatada, who said: "Some of them said: the lamam is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Abu Kurayb and Yaʿqub narrated to us, both saying: Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Abi ʿAruba narrated to us, from Qatada, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The lamam is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: al-Dahhak said, concerning "except for minor faults": "Everything between the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter is the lamam, which Allah forgives."

Al-Tabari's commentary (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 53, verses 31–32 (part 2 of 2):

The most correct of the opinions on this matter, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said that "illa" (except) carries the meaning of the disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category), and that the meaning of the statement regarding ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the grave immoralities, except for minor faults﴾ is: [they avoid] what falls short of the major sins and short of the immoralities that entail legal punishments (hudud) in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, for that is forgiven for them. This, in my view, is like the statement of His, exalted is His praise: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾. So He promised, exalted is His praise, that avoiding the major sins brings pardon for what is less than them among the misdeeds, and that is the minor fault (al-lamam) of which the Prophet ﷺ said: "The eyes commit adultery, the hands commit adultery, the feet commit adultery, and the private part either confirms that or denies it." That is because there is no legal punishment for anything short of the penetration of the private part into the private part. This is the pardon from Allah in this world concerning the servant's punishment for it, and Allah, exalted is His praise, is too generous to take back what He has pardoned, as has been related from the Prophet ﷺ. And al-lamam in the speech of the Arabs means approaching something. Al-Farra' mentioned that he heard the Arabs say: "He struck him with what approaches killing" (ma lamm al-qatl), meaning a blow that approaches killing. [[This expression is among what al-Farra' related from the Arabs; he said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "And I heard the Arabs ... etc.," and what follows it, meaning a blow approaching killing.]] He said: "And I heard from another: alamma yaf'alu," in the sense of "kada yaf'alu" (he almost did).
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knows you best since He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers. So do not attest to your own purity; He is most knowing of who fears Him﴾ (32).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿is vast in forgiveness﴾: His pardon is wide for the sinners whose sins have not reached the immoralities and the major sins. Allah, exalted is His praise, informs His servants by this statement that He forgives minor faults, of the kind we have described, for those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities.

As related:
⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His statement ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾: "He has forgiven that for them."
* *
And His statement ﴿He knows you best since He produced you from the earth﴾:
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Your Lord knows best who among you is a believer and who is a disbeliever, who is good and who is bad, who is obedient and who is disobedient, when He originated you from the earth, creating you from it through the creation of your father Adam from it, and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers, meaning: when you were embryos not yet born, and after you had become men and women.

The interpreters have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His statement ﴿He knows you best since He produced you from the earth﴾: he said: "Like His statement ﴿and He knows best those who are guided﴾."
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿since He produced you from the earth﴾: "When He created Adam from the earth, then created you from Adam." And he recited ﴿and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers﴾.

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "janin" (fetus) and why it is called janin, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here.
* *
And His statement ﴿So do not attest to your own purity﴾:
He, exalted is His praise, says: Do not testify for yourselves that you are pure and free from sins and disobedience.

As related:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say ﴿So do not attest to your own purity﴾, meaning: "Do not declare them innocent."
* *
And His statement ﴿He is most knowing of who fears Him﴾:
He, exalted is His praise, says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of those of His servants who fear Allah's punishment and thus avoid His disobedience.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 53, verses 31–32 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His words, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good with the best (reward)﴾ [53:31] ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults (lamam)﴾ [53:32].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿To Allah belongs﴾ the dominion over ﴿whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of anything. ﴿He leads astray whom He wills, and He knows best about them.﴾ ﴿So that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did﴾: meaning, so that He may recompense those among His creatures who disobeyed Him, who did evil by their disobedience toward Him, by requiting them with the Fire. ﴿And recompense those who did good with the best﴾: meaning, and so that He may recompense those who obeyed Him and did good by their obedience toward Him in this world, with the best (reward), which is Paradise, by rewarding them with it.

It has been said: this refers to the people of polytheism and the people of faith.

Those who said this:
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿so that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did, and recompense those who did good﴾: "They are the believers."

* *

As for His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins﴾:
That is: those who keep far from the major sins which Allah has forbidden and made unlawful for them, so that they do not approach them. These include associating partners with Allah, and what we have already explained in His words ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove your evil deeds from you﴾ [4:31].

* *

As for His words ﴿and the immoralities﴾:
These are adultery and what is similar to it, for which Allah has prescribed a legal punishment (hadd).

* *

As for His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾:
The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the meaning of "illa" (except) in this place. Some of them said: it carries the sense of the disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category as what precedes). They said: the meaning of the statement is: "those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for the minor faults that they committed in the immoral acts and immoralities during the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) before Islam, for Allah has pardoned them for that and will not hold them to account for it."

Those who said this:
• ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: he said, "except what has already passed."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The polytheists used to do these things in the past, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed ﴿except for minor faults﴾, meaning what they did during the Age of Ignorance." He said: "And the minor faults (lamam) are what they committed of those major sins and immoralities in the Age of Ignorance before Islam, and He forgave them when they embraced Islam."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAyyash, from Ibn ʿAwn, from Muhammad, who said: A man asked Zayd ibn Thabit about this verse, ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "Allah has forbidden you immoralities, whether apparent or hidden."
• Yunus ibn Abd al-Ala related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam said, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The major sins of polytheism and the immoralities of adultery. They abandoned that when they entered Islam, so Allah forgave them what they had committed of it and done of it before Islam."

Some scholars of the Arabic language, who direct the interpretation of "illa" in this place to this aspect that I have mentioned from Ibn Abbas, said in explaining it: "It is not permitted for them to commit minor faults, and it is neither among the immoralities nor among the major sins. An exception may be made of a thing from another thing, though it is not part of it, on the basis of an implied reference to something from which one has refrained. Its meaning is: except that a person may commit something that is neither immorality nor a major sin." He said, quoting the poet:

*And a land in which there is no companion, except the yaʿafir (gazelles) and except the ʿis (camels)*

[[The verse is one of the examples cited by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Quran (folio 231), who said, regarding the words of Allah (those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities except for minor faults): "It is not permitted for them to commit minor faults, and it is neither among the immoralities nor among the major sins. An exception may be made of a thing from another thing, though it is not part of it, on the basis of an implied reference to something from which one has refrained. Its meaning: except that a person may commit something which is neither among the immoralities nor the major sins." He said: "And a land in which there is no companion… the two verses." Yaʿafir means gazelles, and ʿis means camels; neither of them is human, so it is as if he said: there is no companion in it, except that there are gazelles and camels in it. Some said: the yaʿfur among gazelles is the red one, and the aʿyas is the white gazelle. End quote. Al-Ayni said in Fara'id al-qala'id: it was said by Jiran al-Awd al-Numayri, whose name is Amir ibn al-Harith. The point of evidence is in "illa al-yaʿafir," since it is an exception from the word "companion" by substitution (badal), even though it is disjunctive, according to the dialect of the Banu Tamim, whereas the people of the Hijaz require the accusative case (for disjunctive exceptions). Yaʿafir is the plural of yaʿfur, which is the young of the wild cow, and ʿis is the plural of ʿaysa', which are white camels whose whiteness is mixed with some reddish tint. End quote. Al-Farra said in Maʿani al-Quran (folio 316), regarding His words "except for minor faults": "It means: except what is close to small sins." He said: "I heard from some Arabs: alamma yafʿalu (he almost did), in the sense of kada yafʿalu (he was about to do)." Al-Kalbi mentioned with his chain that it is a glance without deliberate intent, so it is a minor fault (lamam) and is forgiven; but if he repeats the glance, it is no longer a minor fault, it is a sin. End quote.]]

The yaʿafir are gazelles, and the ʿis are camels, and they are not people; so it is as if he said: there is no companion in it, but there are gazelles and camels in it. Some said: the yaʿfur among gazelles is the red one, and the aʿyas is the white one.

Many exegetes said something similar to this view.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, that Ibn Masʿud said: "The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the lips is kissing, the adultery of the hands is seizing, and the adultery of the feet is walking. The private part confirms this or denies it. If one advances with his private part, he is an adulterer; otherwise it is a minor fault (lamam)."
• Ibn Abd al-Ala related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "I have not seen anything more similar to the minor fault than what Abu Hurayra said from the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Allah has written for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which will inevitably befall him. The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speech, the soul desires and longs, and the private part confirms this or denies it.'"
• Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Muawiya narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim, from Masruq, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "If it precedes, it is adultery; if it follows, it is a minor fault."
• Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Shaʿbi about the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is what falls short of adultery." Then he mentioned to us from Ibn Masʿud, who said: "The adultery of the eyes is what they look at; the adultery of the hand is what it touches; the adultery of the foot is where it walks; and the actual fulfilment is with the private part."
• Muhammad ibn Maʿmar related to me, saying: Yaʿqub narrated to us, saying: Wuhayb narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Uthman ibn Khuthaym ibn Amr al-Qari narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafiʿ, who is called Ibn Lubaba al-Taʾifi, narrated to me, saying: I asked Abu Hurayra about the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is the kiss, the squeeze, the glance, and the intimate contact; when the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, the ghusl (ritual bath) becomes obligatory, and that is adultery."

Others said: rather, this is a genuine exception (istithna' muttasil, an exception of the same category), and the meaning of the statement is: "those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults, unless one commits them and then repents."

Those who said this:
• Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "It is the man who commits an immorality and then repents." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

*"If You forgive, O Allah, You forgive much, and which of Your servants is there who has not committed a fault?"*

[[The verse is by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt (Lisan al-Arab: lamm). He said: "al-ilmam and al-lamm: approaching a sin. It was also said: lamm is what is less than the major sins. In the revealed Book: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾." Alam al-rajul, from lamm, means small sins. Umayya said: "If You forgive, O Allah… the two verses." It is said: it is approaching disobedience without actually committing it. Al-Akhfash said: lamm is approaching sins. Ibn Barri said: the poem belongs to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt. He said: Abd al-Rahman (nephew of al-Asmaʿi) mentioned, from his uncle, from Yaʿqub (Ibn al-Sikkit), from Muslim ibn Abi Tarafa al-Hudhali, who said: Abu Khirash (the Hudhali poet) passed by, running between al-Safa and al-Marwa, saying:

*O God, this is the fifth, if he should complete it: may God complete it, and he has completed it.*
*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*]]

• Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, that he said concerning this verse ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "It is the one who commits a sin and then leaves it." And the poet said:

*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*

• Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buzayʿ related to me, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayra, I think he traced it to the Prophet: ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾. He said: "The lamma (slight lapse) of adultery, then he repents and does not return; the lamma of theft, then he repents and does not return; the lamma of drinking wine, then he repents and does not return." He said: "That is the ilmam."
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "A lamma of adultery or theft or drinking wine, then he does not return."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of Allah ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "A lamma of adultery, or theft, or drinking wine, then he does not return."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: this man commits a lamma of adultery, or a lamma of drinking wine, then he hides it and repents from it."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, concerning "except for minor faults": "One who commits it at the moment; I said: adultery? He said: adultery, then he repents."
• Ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, saying: Maʿmar said: "al-Hasan used to say about the lamm: a man commits a lapse of immorality, then he repents."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ismaʿil, from Abu Salih, who said: "Adultery, then he repents."
• [Ibn Humayd] said: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, concerning "except for minor faults": "That he falls into a fall and then desists."
• Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The lamam is one who commits it once."
• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed me, from al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah, from Amr ibn Shuʿayb, that Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: "The lamam is what is less than polytheism."
• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, saying: Murra narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "A lapse that one commits of sins."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "The man who commits a sin and then turns away from it." He said: "The people of the Age of Ignorance used to circumambulate the House saying:

*If You forgive, O God, You forgive much, and which of Your servants has not committed a fault?*"

Others said, among those who directed the meaning of "illa" to the disjunctive exception: the lamam is what falls short of the worldly limit and the limit of the Hereafter, which Allah has pardoned.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ata, from Ibn al-Zubayr, concerning "except for minor faults": "It is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter."
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "The lamam is what falls short of the two limits: the limit of this world and the Hereafter."
• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Hakam and Qatada, from Ibn Abbas, with the like of this, except that he said: "The limit of this world, and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba informed us, from al-Hakam ibn ʿUtayba, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The lamam is what falls short of the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter, is expiated by the prayers, and it is the lamam, and it is less than every prescribed penalty. As for the limit of this world, it is every punishment which Allah has ordained to be inflicted in this world; and as for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything for which Allah has decreed the Fire and deferred its punishment to the Hereafter."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrima, concerning His words ﴿except for minor faults﴾: "It means: what lies between the two limits; every sin for which there is no prescribed penalty in this world nor punishment in the Hereafter is the lamam."
• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities, except for minor faults﴾: "The lamam is what lies between the two limits, which does not reach the limit of this world nor the limit that entails the Hereafter, for which Allah has made the Fire obligatory for its people, or an immorality for which the prescribed penalty is inflicted in this world."
• Ibn Humayd also narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from Qatada, who said: "Some of them said: the lamam is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Abu Kurayb and Yaʿqub narrated to us, both saying: Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Abi ʿAruba narrated to us, from Qatada, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The lamam is what lies between the two limits: the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter."
• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: al-Dahhak said, concerning "except for minor faults": "Everything between the limit of this world and the limit of the Hereafter is the lamam, which Allah forgives."

Al-Tabari's commentary (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 53, verses 31–32 (part 2 of 2):

The most correct of the opinions on this matter, in my view, is the opinion of the one who said that "illa" (except) carries the meaning of the disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati', an exception not of the same category), and that the meaning of the statement regarding ﴿those who avoid the major sins and the grave immoralities, except for minor faults﴾ is: [they avoid] what falls short of the major sins and short of the immoralities that entail legal punishments (hudud) in this world and punishment in the Hereafter, for that is forgiven for them. This, in my view, is like the statement of His, exalted is His praise: ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance﴾. So He promised, exalted is His praise, that avoiding the major sins brings pardon for what is less than them among the misdeeds, and that is the minor fault (al-lamam) of which the Prophet ﷺ said: "The eyes commit adultery, the hands commit adultery, the feet commit adultery, and the private part either confirms that or denies it." That is because there is no legal punishment for anything short of the penetration of the private part into the private part. This is the pardon from Allah in this world concerning the servant's punishment for it, and Allah, exalted is His praise, is too generous to take back what He has pardoned, as has been related from the Prophet ﷺ. And al-lamam in the speech of the Arabs means approaching something. Al-Farra' mentioned that he heard the Arabs say: "He struck him with what approaches killing" (ma lamm al-qatl), meaning a blow that approaches killing. [[This expression is among what al-Farra' related from the Arabs; he said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "And I heard the Arabs ... etc.," and what follows it, meaning a blow approaching killing.]] He said: "And I heard from another: alamma yaf'alu," in the sense of "kada yaf'alu" (he almost did).
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He knows you best since He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers. So do not attest to your own purity; He is most knowing of who fears Him﴾ (32).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿is vast in forgiveness﴾: His pardon is wide for the sinners whose sins have not reached the immoralities and the major sins. Allah, exalted is His praise, informs His servants by this statement that He forgives minor faults, of the kind we have described, for those who avoid the major sins and the immoralities.

As related:
⁕ Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His statement ﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾: "He has forgiven that for them."
* *
And His statement ﴿He knows you best since He produced you from the earth﴾:
He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Your Lord knows best who among you is a believer and who is a disbeliever, who is good and who is bad, who is obedient and who is disobedient, when He originated you from the earth, creating you from it through the creation of your father Adam from it, and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers, meaning: when you were embryos not yet born, and after you had become men and women.

The interpreters have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said so:
⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His statement ﴿He knows you best since He produced you from the earth﴾: he said: "Like His statement ﴿and He knows best those who are guided﴾."
⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿since He produced you from the earth﴾: "When He created Adam from the earth, then created you from Adam." And he recited ﴿and when you were fetuses in the bellies of your mothers﴾.

We have already explained earlier the meaning of "janin" (fetus) and why it is called janin, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it here.
* *
And His statement ﴿So do not attest to your own purity﴾:
He, exalted is His praise, says: Do not testify for yourselves that you are pure and free from sins and disobedience.

As related:
⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: I heard Zayd ibn Aslam say ﴿So do not attest to your own purity﴾, meaning: "Do not declare them innocent."
* *
And His statement ﴿He is most knowing of who fears Him﴾:
He, exalted is His praise, says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of those of His servants who fear Allah's punishment and thus avoid His disobedience.

**On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of meaning) of His saying, the Exalted:** ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away, and gave a little, and then held back? Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? Or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses, and of Abraham who fulfilled his duty? That no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man shall have nothing except what he strove for.﴾

His exalted remembrance says: "Have you seen, O Muhammad, the one who turned his back on faith in God, and turned away from Him and from His religion, and who gave his companion a little of his wealth, then withheld it and was stingy with him."

It is related that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Some of the polytheists rebuked him, for he had followed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in his religion. The one who rebuked him guaranteed that, if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear for him the punishment of the Hereafter. He did so, and gave the one who rebuked him some of what he had guaranteed, then he was stingy with him and withheld the full amount he had guaranteed.

**Those who said this:**

• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and held back﴾ [more precisely ﴿and was stingy﴾ in the verse's wording]: "al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: he gave a little, then held back."

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿so that he sees﴾: "This is a man who had embraced Islam, and some one who reproached him met him and said: 'You have abandoned the religion of the elders and misled them, and you claimed they are in the Fire. You should have supported them. How will your fathers be treated?' He said: 'I feared the punishment of God.' He said: 'Give me something, and I will bear for you every punishment that is upon you.' So he gave him something. He said: 'Give me more.' So he became difficult, until he gave him something, and wrote him a document and had it witnessed. That is the saying of God ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away, and gave a little, and then held back﴾ — ﴿was difficult﴾ — ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾. This verse was revealed concerning him."

Those learned in the interpretation of the Qur'an said what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿held back﴾.

**Those who said this:**

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and gave a little, and then held back﴾: "He gave a little, then stopped."

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away and gave a little and then held back﴾: he says, "He gave a little, then stopped."

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and gave a little, and then held back﴾: "He stopped, so he gives nothing. Have you not seen the well that is called 'akdat (dried up)?"

It is related that this verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. Some of the polytheists rebuked him, for he had followed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in his religion. The one who rebuked him guaranteed that, if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear for him the punishment of the Hereafter. He did so, and gave the one who rebuked him some of what he had guaranteed, then he was stingy with him and withheld the full amount he had guaranteed.

**Those who said this:**

• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and held back﴾ [more precisely ﴿and was stingy﴾ in the verse's wording]: "al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: he gave a little, then held back."

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾ ... up to His saying ﴿so that he sees﴾: "This is a man who had embraced Islam, and some one who reproached him met him and said: 'You have abandoned the religion of the elders and misled them, and you claimed they are in the Fire. You should have supported them. How will your fathers be treated?' He said: 'I feared the punishment of God.' He said: 'Give me something, and I will bear for you every punishment that is upon you.' So he gave him something. He said: 'Give me more.' So he became difficult, until he gave him something, and wrote him a document and had it witnessed. That is the saying of God ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away, and gave a little, and then held back﴾ — ﴿was difficult﴾ — ﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾. This verse was revealed concerning him."

Those learned in the interpretation of the Qur'an said what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿held back﴾.

**Those who said this:**

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and gave a little, and then held back﴾: "He gave a little, then stopped."

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away and gave a little and then held back﴾: he says, "He gave a little, then stopped."

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and gave a little, and then held back﴾: "He stopped, so he gives nothing. Have you not seen the well that is called 'akdat (dried up)?"

• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and held back﴾: "His giving stopped."

• Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus and Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and held back﴾: "He gave a little, then cut that off."

• He said: Ibn Thawr told us, saying: Ma'mar told us, from 'Ikrimah, the same.

• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, ﴿and held back﴾, meaning: "He was stingy and his giving stopped."

• It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and held back﴾: "He says: his giving stopped."

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and held back﴾: "He was difficult. The Arabs say: 'So-and-so dug and then held back (akdā)', meaning when he reached the hard rock (al-kadya), which is when a man digs in soft ground and then a rock faces him, so he stops (yukdī). It is said: 'He has held back a holding back (akdā kadā'an)'. And 'his fingernails and fingers were stiffened (kudiyat) severely' — shortened (manquṣ) — when they became hard, and 'his fingers were stiffened' when they became unable to work anything. And 'the plant held back' (kadā al-nabt) when its growth became little, whether it is pronounced with a hamza or without." Some scholars of the Arabic language said: "The word akdā is derived from kudyat al-rikiyya, which is digging until one despairs of water; then it is said: 'We have reached its hard rock (kudyatuhā).'"

* *

On His saying ﴿does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees?﴾

His exalted remembrance says: "Does this one, to whom his companion guaranteed that he would bear for him the punishment of God in the Hereafter, have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees the reality of his words and his fulfilment of what he promised?"

* *

On His saying ﴿or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses﴾

His exalted remembrance says: "Or has this guaranteed party not been informed, regarding bearing for him the punishment of God in the Hereafter, by what is in the scrolls of Moses son of 'Imran (peace be upon him)?"

* *

On His saying ﴿and of Abraham who fulfilled (wafā)﴾

He says: "And [what is in the scrolls of] Abraham, who fulfilled what he was sent with to those to whom he was sent."

Then the interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "who fulfilled." Some said: it is his fulfilment of what his Lord charged him with, of conveying His messages, and this is ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾.

**Those who said this:**

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata', from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "Before Abraham, they would seize the close kinsman for the sin of the close kinsman, until Abraham came, and [the revelation] reached ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, and no one is to be taken to account for the sin of another."

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from 'Ikrimah, regarding ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "They said: these verses reached him, ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾."

• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "He fulfilled the obedience of God, and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creatures."

It was said by 'Ikrimah: "He fulfilled these ten verses, ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ ... until [the verse] reached ﴿and that to Him is the final creation﴾."

• Ibn 'Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "He fulfilled the obedience of God and His messages to His creatures."

• Yahya ibn Talha al-Yarbu'i told me, saying: Abu Bukayr told us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "He conveyed what he was commanded."

• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "He conveyed."

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "He fulfilled: he conveyed the messages of his Lord, he conveyed what he was sent with, as a man conveys what he was sent with."

Others said: rather, he fulfilled what he saw in a dream of slaughtering his son. They said that the words ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ are from what is postponed in meaning but placed first; and they said: the meaning of the speech is: "Or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses, that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and of what is in the scrolls of Abraham who fulfilled."

**Those who said this:**

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: he says: "Abraham, who completed obedience regarding what he did with his son when he saw the vision, and what is in the scrolls of Moses is ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a informed me, from Abu Sakhr, from al-Qurazi, who was asked about this verse ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾, and he said: "He fulfilled by sacrificing his son."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that he fulfilled all the laws of Islam to his Lord.

**Those who said this:**

• 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabawayh told us, saying: 'Ali ibn al-Hasan told us, saying: Kharija ibn Mus'ab told us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Islam has thirty shares. No one was tested with this religion and established it except Abraham, and God said ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾, so God wrote for him a quittance from the Fire."

• al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "what was imposed upon him."

Others said: he fulfilled what has been related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the report that:

• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Rushdin ibn Sa'd told us, saying: Ziyan ibn Fa'id told me, from Sahl ibn Mu'adh, from Anas, from his father, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "Shall I not inform you why God named Abraham His friend, 'who fulfilled'? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ﴿So glorified be God when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning ...﴾ until he finished the verse."

Others said: rather, he fulfilled his Lord's work of his day.

**Those who said this:**

• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyya told us, saying: Isra'il told us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, regarding ﴿and Abraham who fulfilled﴾: "Do you know what 'fulfilled' means?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled the work of his day: four rak'ahs during the daytime."

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is the saying of the one who said: he fulfilled all the laws of Islam and all that he was commanded of obedience, because God, the Exalted, reported of him that he fulfilled, so the report of his fulfilment of all obedience is general, and He did not single out some of it over others.

If someone says: "But He specified this by His saying 'who fulfilled' with ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, for that is among what God, may His praise be exalted, reported to be in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham, not among what was specified by the report that he fulfilled." Yet fulfilment is general. And if the two reports we have mentioned, or one of them, were authentically from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), we would not depart from saying it to anything else; but in their chains of narration there is a matter that requires scrutiny for their sake.

* *

On His saying ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾

As for ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear﴾ in the interpretation we have given, it is in the genitive position as a response to the particle "mā" in His saying ﴿or has he not been informed of what is in the scrolls of Moses﴾. By His saying ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ He means something other than it; rather, every sinner's sin is upon herself alone.

We have already explained the interpretation of this, through the differences of scholars regarding it, previously.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said what we have said regarding this.

**Those who said this:**

• Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muharibi told us, saying: Abu Malik al-Janbi told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid told us, from Abu Malik al-Ghifari, regarding His saying ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and that man shall have nothing except what he strove for﴾, up to His saying ﴿from the former warnings﴾: "This is in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses."

Rather, what is meant by His saying ﴿that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ is: the one who guaranteed to al-Walid ibn al-Mughira that he would bear for him the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is: "Has not the speaker of this statement, and the one who gave this guarantee, been informed by what is written in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham: that no sinner shall bear the sin of another? ﴿And that man shall have nothing except what he strove for﴾." He, may His praise be exalted, says: "Has he not been informed that no doer is recompensed except for his deed, whether it be good or evil?"

As:

• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and that man shall have nothing except what he strove for﴾, and he recited ﴿Indeed, your striving is diverse﴾: "Your deeds."

It has been related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "This verse is abrogated (mansūkha)."

• 'Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and that man shall have nothing except what he strove for﴾: "God then revealed after this ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith — We shall join their descendants with them﴾, and so He admitted the children into Paradise by the righteousness of their fathers."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 53, verses 40–44:

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that his striving will be seen (40). Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense (41). And that to your Lord is the final destination (42). And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep (43).﴾

His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿And that his striving will be seen﴾: meaning, may His remembrance be exalted, that the deed of every doer will be seen by him on the Day of Resurrection, when he arrives at the Resurrection with the recompense for which he is repaid, whether good or evil. No one is taken to account for the punishment of a sin other than his own, and no one other than the doer is rewarded for his righteous deeds. What is specifically meant by this is one who turned back from his Islam, relying on the guarantee of his companion to bear his punishment for him: that his guarantee will not benefit him, nor will it avail him anything on the Day of Resurrection, because every doer is held accountable for his own deed.

* *

And His saying ﴿Then he will be recompensed with the fullest recompense﴾

means: then he will be rewarded for that striving with the fullest reward. He, may His praise be exalted, said ﴿the fullest﴾ because it is the most complete of the recompense that He promised His creation for it. The pronoun in His saying ﴿he will be recompensed﴾ refers to "striving" (al-sa'y), and it is to it that it returns.

* *

And His saying ﴿And that to your Lord is the final destination﴾

means, may His remembrance be exalted, saying to His Prophet ﷺ: and that to your Lord, O Muhammad, is the ending and return of all His creation, and it is He who will recompense all of them for their deeds, the righteous and the wicked, the good-doers and the evildoers.

* *

And His saying ﴿And that it is He who makes laugh and makes weep﴾

means, may His remembrance be exalted: and that your Lord is He who makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise by their entering it, and makes the people of the Fire weep in the Fire by their entering it, and makes laugh whomever He wills of the people of this world, and makes weep whomever He wishes to make weep among them.

The interpretation of the words of the Exalted: ﴿And that it is He who causes death and gives life (44).﴾

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And that it is He who created the two mates, the male and the female, from a drop when it is emitted﴾ (45–46) ﴿and that upon Him is the second creation﴾ (47)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And that it is He who causes to die whoever among His creatures dies, and He who gives life to whoever among them lives. By His words ﴿gives life﴾ He means breathing the spirit into the dead drop, making it alive by placing the spirit within it.

* *

And His words ﴿and that it is He who created the two mates, the male and the female, from a drop when it is emitted﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And that it is He who originated the creation of the two mates, the male and the female, and made them two mates, because the male is a mate of the female and the female is a mate of the male, so they are two, each one being a mate of the other.

* *

And His words ﴿from a drop when it is emitted﴾

The word "min" (from) is connected to "created." Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: He created that from a drop when the man and the woman emit it.

* *

And His words ﴿and that upon Him is the second creation﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And that upon your Lord, O Muhammad, is that He creates these two mates after their death, and renews for them in their graves the other creation, which is their restoration alive as a new creation, just as they were before their death.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And that it is He who enriches and grants contentment﴾ (48) ﴿and that it is He who is Lord of Sirius﴾ (49) ﴿and that it is He who destroyed the first ʿĀd﴾ (50) ﴿and Thamūd, and spared none﴾ (51)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And that your Lord is He who enriches whoever He enriches among His creatures with wealth, and grants them contentment, giving him a store of property and assets.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding its interpretation, and some of them said what we have said about it.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmmara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, regarding His words ﴿enriches and grants contentment﴾: he said: "He enriches with wealth and grants contentment with possessions."

Others said: What is meant by His words ﴿enriches﴾ is: he grants servants.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And that it is He who enriches and grants contentment﴾: he said: "enriches: makes him possess property; grants contentment: makes him have servants."

- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿enriches and grants contentment﴾: he said: "He makes him have servants."

And His words: ﴿And that it is He who destroyed the first ʿĀd﴾

The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and some readers of Basra recited "ʿādan lūlā" with the hamza dropped and the nun of ʿādan made quiescent, so that the lam became part of al-Ūlā, as if it were a doubled lam; and the Arabs do this in such cases, as is transmitted from them by hearing: "qum lān ʿannā," meaning "qum al-āna," they made the mim quiescent when the lam with the alif in al-Ān was vocalized; and likewise you say "ṣum ithnayn," meaning "ṣum al-ithnayn." As for al-Qasim ibn Maʿn, it is related from him, from al-Aʿmash, that he agreed in his recitation of this with the readers of Medina.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is what we have mentioned, the recitation of the Kufans, because that is the eloquent form of Arabic speech; and the recitation of those who were native speakers (ahl al-salīqa) is with clear articulation and emphasis; and the assimilation (idghām) in such a letter and the omission of clear articulation is only permitted for those whose natural disposition and temperament was that of the desert dwellers. - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning what we have mentioned: it is said that ʿĀd al-Akbar, whose descendants Allah destroyed with the wind, was called "the first ʿĀd" because they were destroyed before the later ʿĀd. - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿And that it is He who is Lord of Sirius﴾: he said: "It used to be worshipped in the Jahiliyya."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Lord of Sirius﴾: he said: "Mirzam al-Jawza'."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And that it is He who is Lord of Sirius﴾: "There was a tribe of the Arabs who worshipped al-Shiʿra, this star which you see." Bishr said: he means the star that follows al-Jawza'.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Lord of Sirius﴾: he said: "There were people in the Jahiliyya who worshipped this star called al-Shiʿra."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And that it is He who is Lord of Sirius﴾: "It was worshipped in the Jahiliyya, and He said: Do you worship this and leave its Lord? Worship its Lord." He said: "al-Shiʿra is the blazing star that follows al-Jawza', called al-Mirzam."

* *

And His words: ﴿And that it is He who destroyed the first ʿĀd﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, means by "the first ʿĀd": ʿĀd ibn Iram ibn ʿAwṣ ibn Sam ibn Nuh, and they are the people whom Allah destroyed with a fierce, roaring wind, and it is of them that He spoke in His words ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd, of Iram?﴾. The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Medina and some readers of Basra recited "ʿādan lūlā" with the hamza dropped and the nun of ʿādan made quiescent, so that the lam became part of al-Ūlā, as if it were a doubled lam; and the Arabs do this in such cases, as is transmitted from them by hearing: "qum lān ʿannā," meaning "qum al-āna," they made the mim quiescent when the lam with the alif in al-Ān was vocalized; and likewise you say "ṣum ithnayn," meaning "ṣum al-ithnayn." As for the majority of the readers of Kufa and some Meccans, they recited it by making the nun clear and vocalized with a kasra, and by hamzating al-Ūlā, with a difference in this from al-Aʿmash; his companions narrated from him, other than al-Qasim ibn Maʿn, agreeing with the people of his own city in this. As for al-Qasim ibn Maʿn, it is related from him, from al-Aʿmash, that he agreed in his recitation of this with the readers of Medina.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is what we have mentioned, the recitation of the Kufans, because that is the eloquent form of Arabic speech; and the recitation of those who were native speakers (ahl al-salīqa) is with clear articulation and emphasis; and the assimilation (idghām) in such a letter and the omission of clear articulation is only permitted for those whose natural disposition and temperament was that of the desert dwellers. As for the later-born (al-muwallidūn), their rule is to seek out the most eloquent, sweetest and most established recitations, although the other is permissible and not rejected.

ʿĀd ibn Iram was called "the first ʿĀd" because the Banu Luqaym ibn Hazzal ibn Hazl ibn ʿAbayl ibn Diddi ibn ʿĀd al-Akbar, at the time when Allah sent His punishment upon ʿĀd al-Akbar, were residing in Mecca with their brothers from the ʿAmāliqa, the descendants of ʿAmlīq ibn Lawdh ibn Sam ibn Nuh, and they had not been with their people of ʿĀd in their land, so the punishment that befell their people did not befall them; they are the "later ʿĀd" (ʿĀd al-Ākhira), and they were destroyed afterward.

The destruction of the later ʿĀd came about through some of them oppressing others, so they annihilated one another by killing, as follows:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, concerning what we have mentioned: it is said that ʿĀd al-Akbar, whose descendants Allah destroyed with the wind, was called "the first ʿĀd" because they were destroyed before the later ʿĀd. Ibn Zayd used to say: the first ʿĀd was so called only because it was the first of the nations to be destroyed.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿He destroyed the first ʿĀd﴾: it is said: it is of the first of the nations.

* *

And His words: ﴿And Thamūd, and spared none﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah did not leave Thamūd to remain in their transgression and their rebellion against their Lord, but He punished them for their disbelief and arrogance, and destroyed them.

The readers differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Basra and some of the Kufans recited "wa-Thamūda" with tanwin (ʾijrāʾ, i.e. the diacritic of declension), following the Mushaf, since the alif is written in it; and some of the majority of the Kufans recited it without tanwin. It is mentioned that in the Mushaf of ʿAbd Allah it is without an alif.

The correct position regarding this is that both are well-known recitations, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct, for both are sound in grammar and meaning. We have already explained the story of Thamūd and the cause of their destruction earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 52–54:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And the people of Noah before—indeed they were more unjust and more transgressing﴾ (52)

He, may He be remembered, says: And He destroyed the people of Noah before ʿAd and Thamud, for they were more unjust to themselves, greater in disbelief in their Lord, and more insolent and rebellious against Allah than those whom He destroyed after them of the nations. Their transgression is what Allah described them with, and that they were, by this, more transgressing than the other nations.

As follows:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And the people of Noah before—indeed they were more unjust and more transgressing﴾: No group of people was more unjust and more transgressing than the people of Noah. The Prophet of Allah Noah (ﷺ) called them for nine hundred and fifty years. Whenever one generation perished and another arose, the Prophet of Allah called them, until it was related to us that a man would take his son by the hand and walk with him, saying: "My son, my father walked with me to this same [call], and I was like you on that day, following one another in error and denying the command of Allah."

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed they were more unjust and more transgressing﴾, he said: The Prophet of Allah called them for a thousand years less fifty years.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: [He destroyed] the overturned cities, the one whose upper part was turned to its lower part, and it is the town of Sodom, the people of Lot. Allah hurled it down; He commanded Gabriel (ﷺ), who lifted it from the seventh earth with his wing, then hurled it upside down.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you dispute? (55) This is a warner of the warnings of old. (56) The imminent Hour has drawn near. (57) None other than Allah can disclose it. (58)﴾

He says, "So which of the favours of your Lord will you dispute?" — exalted is His remembrance — meaning: which of the blessings of your Lord, O son of Adam, which He has bestowed upon you, will you doubt, dispute, and argue against? The word "ālāʾ" (favours) is the plural of "ilan." It has three forms in its singular: ilyun, on the pattern of "ʿiliyy"; iliyya, on the pattern of "ʿaliy"; and alan, on the pattern of "ʿala" [[In (al-Lisan: ila) "al-ala'" means blessings. Its singular is "alan" (with a fatha on the hamza and lam), "ilan" (with a kasra and then sukun), and "ila" (with a kasra and then a fatha).]].

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.
