* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, "So which of the favours of your Lord will you dispute?" He said: Which of the blessings of your Lord will you dispute?

* * *

As for His saying, "This is a warner of the warnings of old."

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His saying, majestic is His praise, to Muhammad (ﷺ), "This is a warner of the warnings of old," and describing him as being from the earlier warnings, though he is the last of them. Some said: the meaning is that he is a warner to his people, and the warners before him were warners to their peoples, just as one says: "This is one of the sons of Adam, and one of the people."

Those who said that:

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding "This is a warner of the warnings of old," he said: Muhammad (ﷺ) warns just as the messengers before him warned.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying, "This is a warner of the warnings of old": He was sent only with what the messengers before him were sent with.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Shurayk, from Jabir, from Abu Jaʿfar: "This is a warner of the warnings of old": He said: It is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: the meaning is other than all of this. They said: its meaning is: "This which I have warned you of, O people, of the events I mentioned to you, that I brought upon the nations before you, is of the warnings which the nations before you were warned of in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses."

Those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il, from Abu Malik, regarding "This is a warner of the warnings of old," he said: From what they were warned of for their people in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.

What I have mentioned from Abu Malik is closer to the interpretation of the verse, because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, mentioned this in the context of the verses which He reported as being in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses; "a warner of the warnings of old" that came to the nations before you as it came to you. Therefore, His saying "This" being a reference to what preceded it in speech is more appropriate and more fitting than any other reading.

* * *

As for His saying, "The imminent Hour has drawn near."

He says: the near one has come near. What is meant is: the Resurrection, which is near to you, O people, has drawn close. It is said of it: "azifa raḥīl fulān" (the departure of so-and-so has drawn near) when it has approached and come close, as the poet of the Banu Dhubyan (Nabigha) said:

"The departure has drawn near, but our mounts have not yet been loosed from our saddles, as if it had already come."

And as Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr said:

"Youth has departed and gray hair has drawn near, and I see no successor to departed youth."

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

* ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, "The imminent Hour has drawn near" — it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah has magnified and warned His servants of.

* Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, both saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "The imminent Hour has drawn near," he said: The Hour has drawn near.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "The imminent Hour has drawn near," he said: The Hour. "None other than Allah can disclose it."

* * *

As for His saying, "None other than Allah can disclose it."

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: there is no one to disclose the imminent one that has drawn near, which is the Hour that has approached, apart from Allah. He says: it will not be revealed and established except by Allah's establishing it, and its disclosure is beyond anyone other than Him from His creation, for He has not informed any angel brought near or any prophet sent of it. It was said: "kāshifa" is feminine, and it carries the meaning of disclosure, as in: "So do you see any remnant of them?" meaning: do you see any survival for them; as in: "the consequence, and what is his prohibition," and as in: "There is no denial for its occurrence," meaning denial; and "You will not cease to discover treachery from them," meaning betrayal.

Some said: the meaning is that he is a warner to his people, and the warners before him were warners to their peoples, just as one says: "This is one of the sons of Adam, and one of the people."

Those who said that:

* Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding "This is a warner of the warnings of old," he said: Muhammad (ﷺ) warns just as the messengers before him warned.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying, "This is a warner of the warnings of old": He was sent only with what the messengers before him were sent with.

* Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Shurayk, from Jabir, from Abu Jaʿfar: "This is a warner of the warnings of old": He said: It is Muhammad (ﷺ).

Others said: the meaning is other than all of this. They said: its meaning is: "This which I have warned you of, O people, of the events I mentioned to you, that I brought upon the nations before you, is of the warnings which the nations before you were warned of in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses."

Those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il, from Abu Malik, regarding "This is a warner of the warnings of old," he said: From what they were warned of for their people in the scrolls of Abraham and Moses.

* * *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, "The imminent Hour has drawn near," he said: The Hour. "None other than Allah can disclose it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 53, verses 59–62:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse? And you laugh and do not weep? While you are sāmidūn (proud and heedless). So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him].﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the polytheists of Quraysh: "Do you wonder at this Qur'an, O people, that it has been sent down to Muhammad (ﷺ), and do you laugh at it mockingly, and not weep over the threat it contains for the people of disobedience to Allah, while you yourselves are among the people of His disobedience?" ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾ means: you are heedless of the lessons and the reminder it contains, turning away from its signs. It is said to a man, "Leave us your sumūd," meaning, "Leave us your amusement." From this it is said: samada fulān yasmudu sumūdan (so-and-so was sāmid, meaning he was diverted in play).

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken, though their wording of the expression differed. Some of them said: "Heedless." Some said: "Singing." Some said: "Turning away the face in pride (mubarṭimūn)."

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿sāmidūn﴾: he said, "It is singing. When they heard the Qur'an they would sing and play. It is the dialect of the people of Yemen; the Yemeni says: usmud!"

- ʿAlī narrated to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Heedless."

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Heedless."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It is Yemeni: usmid, taghunn lana (sing for us)."

- Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Ashja'ī narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It is singing, and it is Yemeni; they say: usmid lanā, meaning: sing for us."

- He said: ʿUbayd Allah al-Ashja'ī narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ḥakīm ibn al-Daylam, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "They used to pass by the Prophet (ﷺ) proudly. Have you not seen the stallion among the camels, resting in its pen after drinking, with its head raised high?" [[ʿaṭanan: i.e., kneeling in its pen after having drunk. Shāmikhan: raising its head.]]

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatadah, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Heedless."

- Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "They used to pass by the Prophet (ﷺ) angrily, mubarṭimīn." ʿIkrimah said: "It is singing in Ḥimyarite."

- He said: al-Ashja'ī and Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: "It is al-barṭamah."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Al-barṭamah."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us; and al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Al-barṭamah."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The sāmidūn: those who sing in Ḥimyarite."

- al-Ḥārith narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥasan narrated to us, saying: Warqāʾ narrated to us, Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated to us, from Mujāhid, who said: ʿIkrimah used to say: "The sāmidūn sing in Ḥimyarite," without mention of Ibn ʿAbbas.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿sāmidūn﴾: i.e., heedless.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Heedless."

- It was reported to me from al-Ḥusayn, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾: "al-sumūd is play and amusement."

- Ḥumayd ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Fiṭr, from Abū Khālid al-Wālibī, from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: he saw them standing, waiting for the imam, and said: "What is wrong with you, sāmidūn?"

- Ibn Sinān al-Qazzāz narrated to me, both saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿImrān ibn Zāʾidah ibn Nushayt, from his father, from Abū Khālid, who said: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, came out to us while we were standing, and said: "What is wrong with me seeing you sāmidīn?"

- He said: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Maṭar, from Zāʾidah, from Abū Khālid, with the like of it.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Abū Maʿshar, from Ibrāhīm, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "The people standing before the imam comes."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from ʿImrān al-Khayyāṭ, from Ibrāhīm, concerning people waiting for prayer standing; he said: "It used to be said: that is sumūd."

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from Layth and al-ʿAzramī, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "al-barṭamah."

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Mihrān narrated to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾, he said: "Singing in Yemeni: usmud lanā."

- Yūnus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And you are sāmidūn﴾: "The sāmid is the heedless one."

- Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: "They disliked standing when the muezzin called to prayer while the imam was not present, and they disliked waiting for him standing. It used to be said: that is sumūd, or from sumūd."

* *

As for His saying ﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him]﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "So prostrate to Allah, O people, in your prayers, rather than to anyone else among the gods and rivals; and worship Him alone, to the exclusion of others, for worship should belong to none but Him. So devote worship and prostration to Him, and do not make any partner to Him in your worship of Him."

End of the commentary on Surah al-Najm.
